Guides

Travel-time uncertainty

2 min readSource

On this page

Use reserves in a routing requestCalibrate probabilities before offering themReproduce the implemented contract

VIGO supports explicit time reserves that change which journey is chosen. It does not estimate an on-time probability, a travel-time distribution from delays, or a calibrated confidence interval: scheduled and admitted realtime times are point estimates. For variation due to departure time and planned frequencies, see Monte Carlo.

Use reserves in a routing request

ControlApplies toMeaning
minimumTransferBufferMinutesTransit Route and Matrix, either directionExtra minutes before each later boarding, after walking and published minimums
arrivalBufferMinutesArrive-by transit Route and MatrixPlan against a deadline this many minutes earlier

Both are integers 0–60, default 0. A positive arrival reserve needs a deadline at least as large as the reserve and a horizon exceeding it by at least one minute; the earliest departure stays the one implied by the original deadline and horizon. Via points reject a positive reserve, because composing segments would apply it repeatedly; Walk, Drive, Reach and native operations reject an arrival reserve.

For Harvard Square to South Station, save reserved-arrival.json:

JSON
{
  "origin": {"coordinate": [-71.11902, 42.37334]},
  "destination": {"coordinate": [-71.05524, 42.35227]},
  "serviceDate": "2026-10-05",
  "time": "09:00",
  "timePreference": "arrive_by",
  "maxTransfers": 3,
  "horizonMinutes": 120,
  "minimumTransferBufferMinutes": 3,
  "arrivalBufferMinutes": 5
}
Shell
vigo route --city ./boston --request reserved-arrival.json

VIGO plans arrival by 08:55, allows departure no earlier than 07:00, and requires three extra minutes at each change. These are illustrative preferences, not an MBTA delay estimate, and a tighter request can legitimately find no journey.

Route clocks still describe the chosen timetable journey, and a Matrix duration keeps its deadline-minus-departure definition. diagnostics.timeReserves in the trace records both deadlines, both margins and calibratedProbability: false. A transfer reserve can absorb some lateness, but it does not model early departures, missed-connection recovery, crowding, cancellations, correlated delays or uncertain walking.

Calibrate probabilities before offering them

GTFS-Realtime StopTimeEvent.uncertainty has no defined statistical meaning, and an omitted value means unknown. It must not become a standard deviation or a 90% interval without a validated, provider-specific model. See the GTFS Realtime reference.

A calibration study would keep historical forecasts and outcomes, match the exact feed revision and trip, estimate errors by route, direction, time of day and lead time, and validate on later dates. For Boston, the MBTA LAMP exports are a possible input; VIGO does not download or fit them. Delays on one vehicle or corridor are correlated, so multiplying transfer probabilities does not give a journey probability.

Reproduce the implemented contract

npm run check:standalone (test/check-standalone-parity.mjs, test/check-standalone-http.mjs and test/check-service-calendar-boundaries.mjs) and the recorded corpus case route-arrive-by-reserve (npm run check:corpus) cover the reserve on Route and Matrix, invalid values, HTTP requests and service-date boundaries. They establish modeled feasibility, not on-time performance.

PreviousMonte Carlo and accessibilityNextShow fares
Guides

Published fares on itineraries

1 min readSource

Route shows boarding prices from the imported GTFS feed. In Studio, expand a leg's fare for product names, payment methods and the agency's fare link; JSON Results carry the same data in each transit leg's fare.

These are prices for a new boarding, not an optimized journey fare. Multi-leg journeys deliberately have no total, because transfers, discounts, passes and existing tickets change what a rider pays. A missing price does not mean free travel, and price never affects route choice.

Data and matching

The importer keeps fare tables and their references in an optional fare_catalogs table that travels with the City. Cities built before fares were added need their GTFS reimported.

  • Fares v2 takes precedence when fare_products.txt exists. Matching uses networks, areas, rule priorities, timeframes and the default rider category. MBTA's transfer_only extension is honored, so a free-transfer product never becomes a free new boarding.
  • Fares v1 supports flat, route and origin–destination zone prices. Zone-traversal (contains_id) rules stay unpriced.
  • Timeframes use the local date and time at the validation stop, including daylight-saving changes and times after midnight.
  • Ambiguous networks, conflicting products, missing references and unsupported conditions stay unpriced. An unreadable fare catalog never discards a route.
  • Transfer totals, joined fare legs, passes, non-default rider categories and fare-based routing are not implemented.

Matching follows the GTFS Schedule reference. No agency prices are built into VIGO. Fares are looked up only after the route is chosen, so they never slow a search. node test/check-gtfs-fares.mjs holds the public regressions.

PreviousAdd time reservesNextInspect a saved Result

Inspect a saved Result

1 min readSource

Open a JSON Result from the engine, the compiler or the HTTP API. The viewer shows its status and main answer, draws a journey timeline, a matrix table or a Reach raster, and keeps the source JSON beside it. Files are read on your device and never uploaded; the viewer accepts up to 25 MiB.

Route uses journey, Matrix uses durationsSeconds, and Reach uses surface.valuesSeconds or map-only areas. Durations are seconds, and null means unreachable. Keep geometry qualifications and warnings with the answer.

Python's Result.to_dict() keeps its own minute-valued payload; read it with the Python Results guide. The viewer accepts public engine schemas only.

Studio

VIGO Studio

6 min readSource

On this page

Settings and documentationOpen a CityNetworkRoutePlanChoose a networkJourney choicesSave a journeyRecentAnalyzeReachScenariosCityData sourcesPreferencesStudio troubleshootingPlayback shows no tripsAn access path crosses a blockA date is rejectedA loading indicator is not advancing

VIGO Studio puts Network, Route, Analyze and City views over the same routing engine. It keeps its own project library and works offline once a City is imported.

Settings and documentation

Open Settings → Documentation from the City library or the sidebar to read this guide offline. Press / to search; links to external pages open in your browser. Reading documentation does not open a City.

Open a City

Select a project in the Studio library and import GTFS and OSM. Rebuild when the feed or street extract changes. Studio stores projects in its own library format and cannot open City directories built by the compiler in this release. Opening a City prepares walking; driving opens when you select Drive. Background tasks shows preparation progress.

Network

Use Network for reporting coverage and service events, and Routes for trip times, station boards and line views. Network and Routes explains playback, live timing and added service.

Route

Plan

Pick an origin and destination on the map. Add point inserts a via point before the destination, up to eight points in total; click a row to pick it again, use the arrows to reorder it, or remove it. Reverse flips the order. You can also type a coordinate command in Search VIGO, such as route 38.90, -77.05 to 38.91, -77.03 at 08:00, then choose Plan this journey. The route form does not search place or station names.

Choose a travel mode. Realtime transit departs now; Scheduled shows the date, time and depart-at or arrive-by controls. Transfer caps are disabled while via points are present. Rerun route submits the same points again, and New route clears them.

Choose a network

Network chooses what a transit route runs on: the City timetable, one imported timetable, or a saved scenario. Selecting one feed uses its own prepared store and mixes in no other feed. A scenario route uses its timetable group's schedule with removed routes canceled and planned lines added; planned lines run on their stated headway and hours, and new planned stops are reached on foot. Rides on planned service are labeled Planned. Realtime is unavailable while a scenario is chosen. A project may set defaultRoutingFeedId in its Studio metadata to choose the default network.

Journey choices

Sort journeys by Earliest, Fewer transfers or Less walking. Each card shows arrival, total time from your requested departure, transfers, walking, and its trade-off against the earliest arrival. Sorting keeps the selected journey and does not search again; arrow keys, Home and End select another, and Details opens its itinerary.

Later departures add the engine's ranked search at the requested time to the window: up to 64 candidate vehicle chains within fifteen minutes of the earliest arrival, of which at most ten are shown, distinct lines and stops first. A journey is removed when another leaves no earlier, arrives no later, walks no more and boards no more, in the whole minutes Studio shows. Services are grouped only when their stops, ride geometry and access paths match. This is a bounded search, not every possible itinerary.

With Arrive by, Route options offers Exact time or Earlier arrivals. Earlier arrivals searches each deadline in the 20 minutes before the requested arrival and lists up to five distinct journeys, the latest departure first, plus a walk when possible. A deadline close to midnight searches the previous service day.

Save a journey

Choose a format beside Save in the journey details. JSON keeps the plan, diagnostics and a summary separating initial wait, journey duration and total elapsed time. Markdown is a readable itinerary whose clocks can exceed 23 hours. GeoJSON keeps leg geometry and its source. CSV records each leg's trip and service-clock times; clock_service_date names the midnight those minutes count from. Saving never reruns the query. Save all keeps every completed alternative, including those beyond the five visible cards.

Recent

Reopen recent Route Results for the current City revision, with their request, status, warnings and timing.

Analyze

Reach

Choose an origin on the map, or use Choose origin to search imported stops by name or ID or to enter coordinates. Run Reach, then switch between Reachable area, Reached streets and cutoffs; changing the displayed cutoff reuses the Result. Arrive by maps where a destination can be reached from by a deadline; the clock becomes the Deadline.

With street sampling, the map also shades the land beside reached streets: each cell within a straight walk of 100 m takes its fastest nearby street plus that walk, never across mapped water, so the area narrows where time runs out and land farther from every reached street stays empty. The inspector labels these values as off-street estimates. Shading is display only; area metrics and the saved raster keep the street samples.

Click a destination to see its estimate and request a journey there; with the map focused, Enter inspects its center. The journey keeps the analysis origin, date, time, timetable and limits. Planned service changes affect the scenario map but are not rebuilt in the destination journey; the panel labels the difference.

Save offers the full JSON, the selected cutoff's area geometry, or a CSV summary. total_processing_ms measures the whole analysis; area_source distinguishes an exact-cutoff area from a display-raster calculation.

Scenarios

Studio saves scenarios and timetable groups in the City folder, in .vigo/scenarios.json, shortly after each edit. They survive restarts and reimports and travel with the City; a scenario naming a route a reimport removed reports it when run. A copy saved from another window is never overwritten. Road tracing follows the City's streets between the ordered stops; a disconnected segment is explained, never drawn as a straight "road". Use the engine, the compiler or Python for Matrix.

City

Data sources

City → Data sources lists GTFS feeds, OSM coverage, counts and warnings. To remove a source, select the trash button, check the name and confirm Delete source. Removing a GTFS feed rebuilds the combined timetable from the rest; removing OSM removes street routing until another import. Your original files are kept, and deletion is unavailable during import or preparation.

Preferences

Choose appearance, storage location and map preferences. The default City folder is ~/Documents/Vigo Projects. On macOS, Studio does not scan the library until you choose Open library folder, when macOS may ask for permission.

Local OSM is the default basemap: main roads, rivers, lakes and coast from the City's own PBF, with no tile service, API key or network connection. Cities imported before the local map index need one fresh OSM import. Online OpenStreetMap and CARTO styles are optional.

Studio troubleshooting

Playback shows no trips

Check the exact service date, calendar.txt, calendar_dates.txt, the selected direction and pattern, and whether the playback time falls between a trip's first departure and last arrival.

An access path crosses a block

Access lines come from OSM streets. Rebuild from current OSM, confirm the point lies within coverage, and inspect the street leg. Studio never replaces a missing street path with a straight jump.

A date is rejected

Use an exact YYYY-MM-DD date inside the feed's service range. Studio applies the same calendar rules as the command line.

A loading indicator is not advancing

Background tasks show measured progress for steps with a known total; the percentage belongs to that step, not the whole import. Steps without a total show elapsed time and the age of the last update. If updates pause, use Reconnect to task: the task may still be running. Confirm that the City folder is readable and writable and that macOS has granted access.

Studio

Network and Routes

3 min readSource

On this page

Read the evidenceInvestigate a conditionInspect a route or stationPatterns and scheduled playbackVehicle timing and line viewAdded serviceEvidence limits

Open Network in VIGO Studio to inspect the City's timetable, live reports and service events. It has Network and Routes tabs; use Route for journeys and Analyze for Reach.

Read the evidence

What you seeWhat it representsHow to use it
Scheduled timeA GTFS arrival or departure on the selected dateThe published plan
Predicted timeA matched, admitted Trip Update for that trip and stopCompare with the same scheduled event
Vehicle positionA reported location at its own observation timeLocate the vehicle; check its age separately
Estimated playbackA position interpolated along the scheduled tripExplore the timetable and geometry
Service eventA computed delay, spacing change or source alert, with timestampsInspect its evidence and age

None of these is a verified history of arrivals, and a missing prediction stays unknown. A vehicle marker or an added trip does not mean Route can use that trip; routing has its own admission rules.

Investigate a condition

  1. Start with coverage. Check the snapshot time, feed freshness and reporting counts in Network. Reporting counts routes with current trip reports; it is not the share of passengers covered.
  2. Follow the route. Open Routes, select the route and read Trip times on the relevant date. Use Stops to confirm direction and pattern, then Updates for service evidence.
  3. Compare the same event. Open the station board or select a vehicle in Line view. Compare arrival with arrival, or departure with departure, at the same stop, with both observation times visible.
  4. Keep the observation. Export observations or Export report keeps the evidence and its timestamps.

Inspect a route or station

Choose a route in Routes to see Trip times; select a trip and date to compare scheduled and predicted times. Stops opens directions and patterns, and Updates opens service evidence. Select a stop for its arrivals board; All routes returns to the catalog. Selection is shared across Network, Routes, the map and the line view; Network map clears it.

Patterns and scheduled playback

A route's Stops view shows directions, patterns, ordered stops, service span and published geometry. Patterns are labeled by their first and last stops. Direction IDs 0 and 1 are feed labels, not compass directions. Times such as 25:10 stay on their GTFS service day.

Scheduled playback is labeled Estimated: vehicles dwell at stops and follow their shape between timed calls, so positions are approximate. Live positions are drawn separately, with a bearing arrow when reported.

Vehicle timing and line view

In Routes, select a route and choose Line view: two tracks show each direction's stops and reported vehicles. Select a vehicle to compare scheduled and predicted arrival and departure at its reported stop. If that stop has no usable timing, Next prediction names a later stop without substituting its time. The browser requests only the selected route or vehicle, every ten seconds.

  • Stop placement follows the Vehicle Position's stop ID, sequence and status; it never snaps to roads or interpolates. Missing or conflicting identities stay unplaced.
  • Arrival comes from the incoming connection and departure from the outgoing one; delay compares the same event at the same stop.
  • Opposite directions share a station list only when their sequences are exact reverses.
  • Branches and repeated stops stay distinct. Skipped stops, missing predictions, duplicates and stale observations never become current timing.

Spacing is schematic: it shows stop order, not distance or headway. The ↔ warning marks both vehicles of a compressed pair.

Added service

Trips declared ADDED or NEW in GTFS-Realtime appear in the line view and Trip times even when absent from the static timetable. Their reported stops supply placement and timing; scheduled times and delays are unavailable. Added-service display does not make a trip available to journey routing.

Evidence limits

Predicted spacing is not measured headway, and forecast changes are not actual vehicle progress. Reporting coverage is not service health. Network inspection does not establish delay causes, recovery forecasts or passenger impacts, and VIGO does not dispatch vehicles or publish messages. npm run check:agency holds the public regressions; matching follows the GTFS Realtime reference.

Deploy and operate

Deploy the routing engine

4 min readSource

On this page

Build and check the imageStart the serviceResource controlsRun without DockerOperate and upgrade

Run the engine as the HTTP service. It opens a prepared City or scenario collection without Node, Python, Studio or an internet connection. Build the City with vigo build, on the server or on a larger build machine, and mount the complete directory read-only.

Build and check the image

From the repository root with Docker installed:

Shell
docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile -t vigo:1.0.0 .

The image contains the engine with this guide embedded, license notices and a Debian glibc runtime, and runs as UID/GID 65532. Its compiler matches rust-toolchain.toml; City data, JavaScript dependencies, desktop bundles and build caches are excluded. Check the image before using it:

Shell
npm ci
npm run build:cli-runtime
npm run check:deployment -- --image vigo:1.0.0

The check builds public synthetic inputs and exercises the real Compose service: a read-only City, authentication, Route, Matrix, Reach, scenario switching, readiness, restart and resource limits, and it confirms that queries never change City files. CI runs it on Linux x64 and ARM64. The small fixture is not a metropolitan memory or latency result: measure your own City and requests before choosing production limits.

Start the service

Make the City directory readable by UID 65532, and keep every referenced directory inside the mounted City or collection.

Shell
export VIGO_IMAGE=vigo:1.0.0
export VIGO_CITY=/absolute/path/to/prepared-city
# Set VIGO_API_TOKEN through your shell or deployment secret store (16+ characters).
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml up -d --wait

The service binds to 127.0.0.1:8080 on the host; put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of it for remote clients. Query endpoints require Authorization: Bearer ...; readiness and this guide are public.

Shell
curl --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:8080/readyz
curl --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/route \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIGO_API_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @route.json
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml logs --tail 50

GET /v1/info reports the City, memory and scenario residency. For a scenario collection, pass scenarioId with each query. The HTTP API lists every endpoint and status code.

Resource controls

Compose defaults to 2 CPUs, 2 GiB of memory and no swap, two native threads, two resident scenarios, and one query worker with a bounded queue. It uses a read-only root filesystem and City mount, drops Linux capabilities, limits processes, and keeps two 5 MB log files.

Compose variableDefaultMeaning
VIGO_IMAGERequiredThe image you built and checked
VIGO_CITYRequiredAbsolute path to the City or collection on the host
VIGO_API_TOKENRequiredBearer token, at least 16 characters
VIGO_LOCAL_PORT8080Loopback port on the host
VIGO_CPUS / VIGO_MEMORY2 / 2gContainer CPU and memory limits
VIGO_MEMORY_SWAPEqual to VIGO_MEMORYMemory plus swap; equal values disable swap
VIGO_THREADS2Threads per query (RAYON_NUM_THREADS)
VIGO_MAX_RESIDENT_SCENARIOS2Collection members kept loaded
VIGO_ENDPOINT_CACHE_MAX_BYTES8388608Endpoint cache budget
VIGO_SHAPE_GEOMETRY_CACHE_MAX_BYTES8388608Shape cache budget
VIGO_MAX_QUEUE8Waiting queries
VIGO_MAX_CONNECTIONS16Open HTTP connections
VIGO_MAX_BODY_BYTES8388608Largest request body
VIGO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS10000Request and response I/O deadline
VIGO_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS30000Queue plus computation deadline

Other engine variables, such as VIGO_RESIDENT_HEAP_BYTES and VIGO_PREPARE, keep their defaults unless you add them to the Compose file. Before raising limits, read Resource limits: extra processes are not a free speedup, and swap is never counted as RAM.

The worker keeps its City and workspaces, puts short queries first, and gives waiting analytical work a bounded turn. A deadline or cancellation stops running work and restarts the worker, and readiness is unavailable meanwhile. A full queue returns 503 instead of accepting unbounded work. Responses are limited to 64 MiB; split large matrices or omit geometry.

GET /healthz checks the HTTP process and GET /readyz the worker. The container runs vigo health against /readyz; the probe loads no City and needs no shell or curl. The restart policy restarts exited containers, not merely unhealthy ones.

Run without Docker

The engine archive runs directly: vigo serve --city ./city --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080, checked with vigo health --port 8080. For a Linux host, install the matching binary, create an unprivileged account, make the City readable, and keep the token in a protected environment file. A systemd unit:

INI
[Unit]
Description=VIGO routing service
After=network.target

[Service]
User=vigo
Group=vigo
EnvironmentFile=/etc/vigo/runtime.env
ExecStart=/opt/vigo/vigo serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
Restart=on-failure
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
PrivateTmp=true
KillMode=control-group

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

Set VIGO_CITY and VIGO_API_TOKEN in the environment file. Stop the service through systemd so its worker stops too. Scale out with several service processes, each with its own City and queue; there is no shared queue, distributed cache or tenant management. The Docker and systemd recipes are deployment examples; the container check above is the tested configuration.

Operate and upgrade

Prepare a new City in a separate directory, check saved requests against it, and switch the image and City together. Never replace files a running service has mapped, and keep the previous image and City for rollback; see Upgrade and rollback. Service benchmarking records startup, first-query and sustained latency, memory and disk use. Stop the service with docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml down; the City stays on the host.

To offer a public journey planner on top of a service, see the public route planner.

Deploy and operate

Resource limits and constrained serving

3 min readSource

On this page

Processes and threadsCapacity-aware defaultsScenario and date switchingSwap is an explicit choiceWhat the checks establish

This page explains how VIGO uses CPU and memory, and how to size a deployment. The Compose defaults suit a 2 CPU, 2 GiB container; environment variables lists every control.

Processes and threads

The HTTP service runs one supervised query worker with bounded admission, deadlines, cancellation and recovery. A query can use several threads (RAYON_NUM_THREADS), and endpoint access searches run on up to four threads, following the available CPUs, Linux quotas and affinity. One query worker and two threads suit a 2 CPU, 2 GiB deployment.

More processes are not a free speedup: each one loads its own City. Python's City.iter_run(queries, workers=2) and the compiler's stream --workers 2 run separate resident processes; measure before adding them. Python caps its one to four workers by CPU affinity, quota and visible memory limits, chooses one worker when memory capacity is unknown, and defaults to workers=1.

Capacity-aware defaults

At startup, the engine reads the smallest of Linux physical memory, cgroup v2 memory.max and memory.high, and cgroup v1 limits, including visible parent limits, and sizes its caches from it. Unlimited values are ignored. Other platforms, and Linux controllers mounted in unusual places, keep the fixed defaults below. Explicit settings always win.

AllocationDefault upper boundShare of detected memory
Endpoint cache, per role64 MiB1/64
Shape geometry cache64 MiB1/64
Inactive timetables128 MiB, growing to twice a retired view1/32, growing to 1/16
HTTP pending request bytes64 MiB1/32
HTTP pending response bytes128 MiB1/16

Caches hold reusable work; shrinking them never changes or truncates an answer. Collections divide the caches among resident members. The loaded City and query scratch are outside these budgets, so small caches do not make a large City fit.

vigo info and GET /v1/info report resourcePolicy.memoryCapacityBytes and swapCountsAsRam. Capacity is a startup sizing input, not free memory or an RSS limit. Restart after changing container limits.

Scenario and date switching

For a collection, read the residency counters in /v1/info before blaming route search for latency. Rising cityOpens and evictions on a repeated scenario sweep mean the resident members exceed VIGO_RESIDENT_HEAP_BYTES, even when VIGO_MAX_RESIDENT_SCENARIOS allows them. Raise the budget only with measured container peaks, leaving room for query scratch, mapped pages and other services. When the heap exceeds its budget, the collection first drops optional timetable caches, then evicts members.

Changing service dates can rebuild a timetable when the inactive-timetable cache is too small. Large scheduled timetables are kept losslessly compressed within the same budget, so more dates fit on a small host. Their keys include the active services, dates and horizon; realtime and linked trips are applied after restoring. The first use of a date still reads SQLite, and eviction remains possible. Trace timings separate linkedCandidatesMs and linkedTripsMs within sourceAndRealtimeMs.

Swap is an explicit choice

The Compose service disables swap by setting memory plus swap equal to memory. To allow 4 GiB of swap beside 2 GiB of RAM, set VIGO_MEMORY=2g VIGO_MEMORY_SWAP=6g; the host must already have the swap. Swap is never counted as RAM when sizing workers or caches. It can hold cold pages under pressure but can make queries much slower.

Record RSS, cgroup current and peak memory, swap, memory events, pressure and latency separately; container memory includes page cache and is not RSS. See the Linux memory-controller documentation.

What the checks establish

npm run check:deployment runs the shipped image and Compose file at 2 GiB with a small synthetic collection, including full geometry, scenario eviction, restart and read-only City integrity. It validates the controls and recovery; it does not show that a regional City fits a given size. Before claiming a deployment budget, measure your own City and workload, including errors and out-of-memory events.

Runtime memory and caching

2 min readSource

On this page

TimetablesCollectionsCaches and scratchMemory ledger

A resident stream or serve process keeps its City, timetables and street indexes ready between requests. This section explains what it keeps and how to account for memory. Resource limits explains how to size a deployment.

Timetables

Opening a City and answering the first transit query for a date prepares that date's timetable, or loads a compiled snapshot (timing.timetableSource: "prepared_snapshot"). Prepared timetables cover at least through 06:00 the next day; longer requests extend coverage in six-hour blocks.

Each City retains up to eight inactive scheduled timetables, so switching back to a date or transfer policy reuses its arrays. The default budget is 128 MiB, or 1/32 of a smaller detected memory; without VIGO_TIMETABLE_CACHE_BYTES, a single City's budget grows to twice the size of a view it retires, up to 1/16 of memory, so a large City keeps its other service day. Setting the variable fixes the budget; 0 disables retention. Least recently used entries are evicted, and oversized entries are not kept. The two latest realtime views are also kept. Calendar rules load once per City, and equal timetable columns are shared across retained dates. In a collection, a member can borrow unused collection budget without evicting another member's dates.

Collections

Members share immutable street arrays and hierarchies by path, and equal timetable columns are shared across members. Stop and trip identities, search indexes, endpoint caches and realtime state stay per member. When maximumResidentScenarios is reached, the least recently used member is evicted before another opens; the street graph stays. VIGO_RESIDENT_HEAP_BYTES also evicts members after a query when the measured retained heap exceeds it; the selected member is always kept, and residentHeapOverBudget reports when it alone exceeds the budget. residency.lastQueryTiming separates selection, opening, execution and retention.

Caches and scratch

Endpoint and shape caches have byte budgets shared by all resident members. Street search scratch is allocated only where a query writes; path scratch above 32 MiB and hierarchy workspaces above 64 MiB are dropped after each query. On Linux with glibc, freed pages are returned after timetable preparation, Matrix and Reach, and after VIGO_IDLE_RELEASE_MS of idleness. Caches hold prepared data and paths, never answers: every query is computed.

The HTTP supervisor forwards the worker's JSON bytes without rebuilding them. Server-Timing's serialize entry measures the supervisor; forwarded results report zero, and serialization in the worker counts in the end-to-end time.

Memory ledger

GET /v1/info (or vigo info) reports a memory ledger: network allocations, query workspaces, caches, SQLite and mapped file lengths, with shared owners counted once in trackedHeapBytes. It also reports timetablePreparations, timetableCoverageEndSeconds, memory.timetableCache (entries, retainedBytes, budgetBytes, hits, evictions) and resourcePolicy (memoryCapacityBytes, swapCountsAsRam). Vector capacities are counted; hash-table and JSON overheads are estimates; mapped file lengths are not resident memory. Record process RSS or PSS and cgroup memory alongside the ledger. sourceArrayBytes counts logical column contents, including shared values; never sum it as exclusive memory.

Public route planner

4 min readSource

On this page

Run the gatewayLimits and securityAddress searchCheck a deployment

The public gateway serves Studio's route planner to the public for a fixed set of prepared Cities: a City selector, typed address search, journey planning and a light or dark appearance, on phones and desktops. It exposes routing only. Management and import APIs, live-feed settings and realtime snapshots are unavailable, so every public journey uses the published timetable. app.vigo.city runs this gateway.

Run the gateway

Build the frontend, run Studio's local API on a loopback address, then start the gateway with a private configuration file:

Shell
npm run build:studio-assets
node src/server/public-routing-gateway.mjs /path/to/private-config.json

To run the gateway outside this checkout, deploy public-routing-gateway.mjs with its siblings address-search.mjs, address-index.mjs and address-index-worker.mjs. The static root holds the built index.html, assets/ and brand images; it must not expose the CLI or server bundles.

JSON
{
  "upstream": "http://127.0.0.1:8787",
  "publicOrigin": "https://routes.example.org",
  "staticRoot": "/srv/vigo/public",
  "port": 8788,
  "maxActive": 2,
  "cities": [
    {
      "cityId": "boston",
      "name": "Boston",
      "timeZone": "America/New_York",
      "bounds": [-72.5, 41, -70, 43.5],
      "searchCenter": [-71.0589, 42.3601],
      "addressIndexPath": "/srv/vigo/search/boston.sqlite",
      "coverage": "Selected transit feeds · Scheduled",
      "warmupRequests": [
        {
          "mode": "bike",
          "origin": { "coordinate": [-71.0589, 42.3601] },
          "destination": { "coordinate": [-71.0754, 42.3473] },
          "bike": { "profile": "balanced", "speedKph": 18 }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
City fieldMeaning
cityId, nameA prepared City in the upstream instance, and its display name
timeZoneIANA timezone; Depart now uses the current time there
boundsRequests outside these bounds are rejected
searchCenterBreaks address-search ties toward the City center
addressIndexPathLocal address index; see Address search
geocoderEndpointOptional HTTPS Photon-compatible geocoder for searches the index cannot answer
coverageA label disclosing partial networks or modeled data
warmupRequestsUp to four route requests run at startup; configure one per offered mode

Up to eight Cities can be listed. Startup loads their catalogs, keeps them resident, and runs the warm-up requests before accepting visitors. A blocked warm-up result still prepares its mode, but does not prove that journeys exist: check representative journeys separately. Restart the gateway after updating prepared data. On the upstream API, set VIGO_NATIVE_CITY_MAX to fit the list and VIGO_NATIVE_CITY_PROCESSES for the host's memory and concurrency. Links can select a City with ?city=boston.

Limits and security

Limits apply across all Cities, per IP address and minute: 30 route and readiness requests, 60 searches and 600 other reads. Keep the gateway on loopback behind a proxy that sets CF-Connecting-IP. Built assets are served as immutable; the page revalidates by ETag and carries a content security policy. Every Result reports scheduled routing provenance.

For app.vigo.city, src/server/public-routing-edge.mjs runs at the edge in front of the gateway. When the routing host cannot be reached, it serves a self-contained offline page with HTTP 503 and no-store, which offers Go to vigo.city and Stay here; /offline shows that page without contacting the host. API failures stay JSON with X-Vigo-Offline: 1. Rate limits and geocoder errors do not trigger the offline page.

Address search

Search suggests places after three characters and a 150 ms pause, through POST /api/projects/:id/address-search, within the selected City's bounds. It supports exact names and house numbers, street abbreviations, place initials and single-letter typos; nearby duplicates collapse, and stations stay distinct from landmarks with the same name. Arrow keys and Enter select a suggestion, and map picking still works if search fails.

Build a City's local index with osmium installed:

Shell
node scripts/build-address-index.mjs --osm city.osm.pbf \
  --output addresses.sqlite --name Boston --bounds '[-72.5,41,-70,43.5]'

Use a complete OSM extract for named landmarks; --places places.json can add an Overpass JSON export made with out center. The builder records source hashes, writes a new file and never changes routing Cities. Keep the index outside the public static directory, and restart the gateway after replacing it. Each City's lookups run on their own worker thread, so a broad search cannot delay routes; a lookup over two seconds counts as no match.

A City with an index answers from it alone, so what people type stays on your host. Set geocoderEndpoint to also ask a Photon-compatible service when the index has no match. A City without an index uses Photon's public demo, which permits reasonable use without an availability guarantee; production volume needs your own geocoder. Remote lookups have an eight-second timeout, two concurrent requests and a one-hour bounded cache, and are canceled when the text changes. Clients cannot choose the geocoder.

Check a deployment

Run npm run typecheck, npm run check:css and npm run check:security. Then, on the deployed site, check City switching, both appearances, address selection, and the route controls and itinerary at phone and desktop widths. The gateway checks cover startup readiness, redaction, allowlists, bounds, shared limits and geocoder failures.

Upgrade and rollback

2 min readSource

On this page

Before changing versionsPrepared City policyValidate, switch and recoverChecks you can run yourself

Keep a running application and its City together until the replacement passes your saved requests. A new release does not by itself make an older City compatible or incompatible; the prepared-data contract decides.

Before changing versions

  1. Save the runtime version, package checksum, capabilities output and City inspection (vigo info --city ./city).
  2. Keep the original GTFS and OSM inputs, their checksums, build options and scenario definitions. A prepared City is not a substitute for its sources.
  3. Keep representative Route, Matrix and Reach requests and their Results, including your transfer, walking and arrive-by settings.

Prepared City policy

VIGO keeps a permanent prepared-data baseline: later readers open published Cities without rebuilding, and standard writers produce Cities the published reference runtime can read. The prepared-data contract defines this promise and its release gate.

Cities older than the supported format are not converted. Rebuild them from the original sources into a different directory:

Shell
vigo build --gtfs feed.zip --osm region.osm.pbf --output ./city-next
vigo info --city ./city-next
vigo route --city ./city-next --request route.json

The runtime checks timetable, transfer, street, access and index formats separately, so the outer vigo.city.v1 manifest is not enough, and editing a format marker cannot migrate contents. Some fixes, such as improved station or wheelchair preparation, apply only to Cities built after them; the release notes say when to rebuild.

Validate, switch and recover

Run the saved requests against the candidate through the interface your application uses. Check schemas, no-journey outcomes, walking geometry, times, boardings and resource use, and test a cold start as well as repeated requests. Start a second service on city-next, check readiness and replay the requests before switching. Roll back by restoring the previous binary and City together; never overwrite a City a service has open.

Checks you can run yourself

From a source checkout with the documented toolchain:

Shell
npm ci
npm run build:cli-runtime
npm run build:standalone
npm run check:correctness
npm run check:public-results
npm run check:portability
npm run package:standalone
python3 test/check-standalone-package.py

These use public synthetic inputs and cover independent verification of the algorithms, difficult routing cases, public schemas, moving a City between machines, and running from the extracted package. They need no private data. A local pass does not show that other platforms pass; release CI runs all four.

Reference

VIGO engine reference

1 min readSource

VIGO 1.0.0 · the vigo executable · request schema vigo.standalone.query.v1 · City format vigo.city.v1

The engine is one native executable. It builds a City from GTFS and OpenStreetMap, opens it read-only and answers Route, Matrix and Reach from the command line, a resident NDJSON stream, or an HTTP service. The City compiler, the routing kernels, the City loader, the HTTP server and SQLite are compiled in; nothing else is needed to build or to query: no Node, Python, browser or network connection.

This page is the complete reference: every command, flag, request field, endpoint and environment variable. It is also the README of the engine archive. For tutorials and explanations, start with the VIGO guide, which the engine serves at http://127.0.0.1:8080/ while vigo serve runs. The public results reference explains every answer, the API schema lists every typed field, and the OpenAPI document describes the HTTP API.

  • Command lineCommands, flags, files and exit codes.
  • Request basicsPoints, clocks, units and the fields every query shares.
  • RouteJourneys, alternatives, via points and departure windows.
  • MatrixTravel times for many origins and destinations.
  • ReachRasters, polygons, contours and street evidence.
  • ScenariosPlanned service changes for one request.
  • Realtime and trafficGTFS-Realtime, Service Alerts and traffic observations.
  • HTTP APIEndpoints, limits, status codes and authentication.
  • Environment variablesEvery variable the engine reads.

Run vigo capabilities before integrating: it reports the version, commands, modes and optional features of the executable you have.

Reference

Engine command line

6 min readSource

On this page

CommandsBuild a CityQuery flagsServer flagsInput, output and exit codes

The guides call the engine vigo. Every command accepts --name value and --name=value. Unknown options, options that do not apply to the command, repeated options and extra positional arguments are rejected. A boolean flag is true when bare (--pretty) and accepts --pretty=true or --pretty=false; --pretty false is not boolean syntax.

Commands

Data commands need a City: --city DIR or the VIGO_CITY environment variable. This includes compare. build and build-scenarios write to --output; help, version, capabilities and health need no City.

CommandPurposeMain input
help, --help, -hPrint the command overviewNone
version, --version, -VPrint the version and runtimeNone
buildCompile GTFS and OSM into a City; see Build a CityGTFS ZIPs, an OSM PBF and an output directory
build-scenariosCompile a collection of Cities that share one street network; see Scenario collectionsA source manifest and an output directory
capabilitiesSupported commands, modes and optional features, as JSONNone
infoIdentity, sources, counts, limitations and memory of the CityCity
routeA journey between ordered placesJSON request or endpoint flags
matrixTravel times between every origin and destinationJSON request
reach, isochroneReachable streets, raster, polygons and contoursJSON request or origin flags
compareChanges between two saved Reach ResultsJSON with before and after
nativeOne low-level kernel operationJSON with operation and input
streamResident NDJSON: one request per input lineCity; requests on stdin
serveResident HTTP serviceCity and server flags
healthAsk a running service whether it is ready, without loading a City--host, --port
traffic-importConvert NDW DATEX II v3 travel times into a traffic snapshotCity and XML files

Commands that start with _ are internal: the HTTP supervisor and Studio's data preparation run them.

Build a City

Shell
vigo build --gtfs feed.zip --osm region.osm.pbf --output ./city
vigo build --gtfs rail.zip --gtfs-scope rail --gtfs bus.zip --gtfs-scope bus \
  --osm region.osm.pbf --output ./city --street-modes walk,drive,bike --prepare-date 2026-10-05
OptionMeaning
--gtfs PATHGTFS ZIP; repeat for several feeds
--gtfs-scope NAMEA unique, stable scope for each --gtfs; defaults to the file name
--osm PATHOSM .pbf covering the City
--output PATHThe City directory to write
--street-modes VALUEwalk,drive (default), walk, walk,bike or walk,drive,bike
--prepare-date YYYY-MM-DDCompile a service date's timetable now; repeat for other dates
--private-access VALUEpublic (default) or endpoints
--wheelchairBuild a strict wheelchair City (walking only, public access)
--wheelchair-streets MODEinferred (default) or verified street evidence for a wheelchair City
--streets-from PATHReuse identical prepared streets from another City
--replaceReplace an existing City

--gtfs, --gtfs-scope and --prepare-date may repeat; other options may appear once. Progress goes to standard error as [gtfs], [osm], [transfers] and [city] lines, and the City manifest (network.json) is printed to standard output. Exit 0 means the City was published; exit 2 reports invalid options or a failed build on standard error. The build is staged beside the output and renamed into place when complete: a failure, Ctrl-C or a termination signal leaves an existing City untouched and removes the unfinished one, and the next build cleans up after a crash. GTFS and OSM compile at the same time when installed memory, free memory and load allow it. Build a City explains inputs, combined feeds and large regions. Feeds with frequency-based trips are always compiled from source at query time, so --prepare-date notes and skips them.

Query flags

Flags override the matching fields of the JSON request. stream applies them to every line, so omit --service-date when lines use different dates.

FlagCommandsMeaning
--city DIRData commandsPrepared City or scenario collection; overrides VIGO_CITY
--routing-store FILEData commands except serve and traffic-importWhen --city names a Studio project's .vigo folder, the timetable store in its routing/ folder to open, such as current.sqlite
--scenario IDinfo, route, matrix, reach, native, streamMember of a scenario collection; omission selects defaultScenario. Sets scenarioId
--request FILEroute, matrix, reach, compare, nativeJSON request; - reads standard input
--output FILEOne-shot commandsSave the JSON instead of printing it; - prints
--prettyOne-shot commandsIndent JSON
--format text|jsonOne-shot commandstext prints a short summary; the default is text in a terminal and JSON otherwise
--diagnostics LEVELQuery commandsnone (default), summary, profile or trace; see public results
--include-geometryQuery commandsRoute geometry is on by default; --include-geometry=false omits it. Matrix geometry is opt-in
--include-limitationsQuery commandsAdd the City's dataset limitations to the Result
--stream-output public|detailedstreampublic Results (default) or the internal vigo.stream.detail.v1 envelope
--service-date YYYY-MM-DDroute, matrix, reach, native, streamService date
--time HH:MM[:SS]route, matrix, reach, streamClock; replaces timeMinutes
--mode transit|walk|drive|bikeroute, matrix, reach, streamTravel mode
--from lon,lat or --from stop:IDroute, reachOrigin
--to lon,lat or --to stop:IDroute, reachDestination; arrive-by Reach takes a destination
--arrive-byroute, matrix, reachArrive by --time; --arrive-by=false restores depart-at
--max-walk KMroute, matrix, reach, streammaxWalkKm
--max-transfers Nroute, matrix, reach, streammaxTransfers
--max-street KMroute, matrixmaxStreetKm
--horizon MINUTESroute, matrixhorizonMinutes
--alternatives NrouteAdditional transit journeys, 0–9
--alternative-ranking pareto|rankedrouteHow alternatives are chosen
--cutoffs 15,30,45reachcutoffsMinutes
--raster-size NreachrasterSize
--radius KMreachextentRadiusKm
--street-edgesreachincludeStreetEdges
--wheelchairroute, matrix, reach, streamRequire the City's strict wheelchair profile; --wheelchair=false rejects a wheelchair City

Other controls, such as transfer buffers, realtime snapshots, scenarios, via points and bicycle preferences, are JSON fields.

Server flags

serve takes --city and these flags:

FlagDefaultRange and meaning
--host ADDRESS127.0.0.1Literal IPv4 or IPv6 address to bind, not a hostname. A non-loopback address requires VIGO_API_TOKEN
--port NPORT, otherwise 80800–65535; 0 selects a free port
--max-body-bytes N83886081024–8388608
--request-timeout-ms N1000050–60000; deadline for reading a request and writing its response
--query-timeout-ms N300001–600000; queueing plus computation
--max-connections N322–256 data requests in progress; four further connections stay open to health, readiness, status and cancellation
--max-queue N80–128 waiting queries
--realtime-poll FILENonePoll GTFS-Realtime feeds; see automatic GTFS-RT polling
--ndw-poll FILENonePoll NDW traffic; see automatic NDW polling

health accepts --host and --port with the same defaults. It prints ready and exits 0 when GET /readyz succeeds within two seconds, and exits nonzero otherwise.

traffic-import accepts --city, --output, --pretty, --format, and:

FlagMeaning
--configuration FILENDW measurement-site configuration, XML or gzip; required
--measurements FILENDW travel-time measurements, XML or gzip; required
--ttl-seconds NValidity of the snapshot; default 300

Input, output and exit codes

A request file or standard input holds one JSON object, optionally preceded by a UTF-8 byte-order mark, up to 8 MiB. --request - reads until standard input closes.

Results go to standard output; progress and errors go to standard error. With --output, the JSON is written to a temporary file in the same directory and renamed into place, so a reader never sees a partial file; an existing file keeps its permissions. The directory must exist.

Exit codeMeaning
0A Result was produced, including status: "not_found"
2Invalid input or a failure; a vigo.error.v1 object is written to standard error

A failed run leaves an existing --output file unchanged: check the exit code before reading it. There is no CSV batch interface in the engine; use Matrix or stream.

Request basics

4 min readSource

On this page

PointsClocks and service datesUnitsCommon fields

The command line, the stream and the HTTP API take the same JSON request. The API schema lists every field with its type, range and default, generated from the engine's request types.

Points

A point is a coordinate, a stop, or both:

JSON
{"coordinate": [-77.05, 38.9]}
JSON
{"stopId": "A"}

Coordinates are [longitude, latitude] in WGS84 degrees: longitude −180 to 180, latitude −90 to 90. A bare [longitude, latitude] array is also a point. A stop can be written {"stop": {"feed": "mbta", "id": "70067"}}, the form Results use, or {"stopId": "70067"}. Stop IDs are exact and case-sensitive; VIGO does not look up names or geocode.

Point objects also accept id, name, label and source, which do not change routing, and the scenario fields editStatus, baselineStopId and baselineStopIndex. A valid stop takes precedence over a coordinate, except with source: "map", which uses the coordinate. Selecting a station includes its prepared platforms; that does not certify a path between every platform.

In a City built from several feeds, an ID can carry its feed scope. Use timetable.identifiers (a native operation) to list the active IDs; a local ID need not be unique in a combined City.

Clocks and service dates

Transit queries need serviceDate (YYYY-MM-DD) and a clock. time is HH:MM or HH:MM:SS with hours 0–71, so 25:10 is 01:10 the next morning on the same service day. timeMinutes (0–4319) is the same clock in minutes; never send both. Street-only queries need a clock but can omit the date.

Clocks are local times in the City's timetable timezone. GTFS service days start at "noon minus twelve hours", so a daylight-saving change keeps every clock on its service day. A Result's journey.clockDate anchors every clock it prints; each transit leg's serviceDate names the day its trip runs. Calendar exceptions apply exactly, and trips from adjacent service days are included where their times overlap the search.

The depart-at timetable search ends at departure plus horizonMinutes; arrive-by searches back to the later of midnight and the deadline minus the horizon. A final walk may finish after the horizon. Drive routing has no travel-time horizon; maxStreetKm bounds it.

Units

QuantityRequestsPublic Results
Distance limitsKilometers (maxWalkKm, maxStreetKm, extentRadiusKm)Meters (distanceMeters)
DurationsMinutes (horizonMinutes, cutoffsMinutes, buffers)Seconds (durationSeconds, valuesSeconds)
ClocksHH:MM[:SS] or minutesHH:MM:SS on the service day
Speedskm/h (walkSpeedKph, bike.speedKph)Not reported

Native operations use seconds and meters unless a field name says otherwise. Internal trace output keeps its own units, named in each field.

Common fields

FieldDefaultValues and meaning
serviceDateRequired for transitExact YYYY-MM-DD; calendars and exceptions select service
serviceDayDerivedweekday, saturday or sunday; must agree with the date
timeRequired unless timeMinutesHH:MM[:SS], hours 0–71
timeMinutes—0–4319; never with time
timePreferencedepart_atdepart_at or arrive_by; depart and arrive are accepted
modetransittransit, walk, drive or bike
maxWalkKm1.20–100. Transit: each access and egress walk. Reach: the walking budget. Drive and Bike: the walk between a point and its road
maxTransfersNo capInteger 0–31; 0 allows one boarding
horizonMinutes4801–2880; Route and Matrix only
maxStreetKm500.05–1000; Walk, Drive and Bike distance limit. Smaller values are rejected, never rounded up
allowStreetTransferstruefalse keeps changes to the same stop or station
minimumTransferBufferMinutes0Integer 0–60, added before each later boarding
arrivalBufferMinutes0Integer 0–60; arrive-by transit Route and Matrix plan against an earlier deadline
requireTransitRidefalseTransit Route and Matrix: require at least one boarding
allowLongWalktrueTransit only: false caps a direct walk by maxWalkKm instead of maxStreetKm
walkSpeedKphCity policy, normally 4.81–8. Walk, Drive and Bike Route and Matrix, and Reach. Transit Route and Matrix reject it
disableCachefalseSkip endpoint and walking-path caches for this request; not a cold-start switch
requireCompleteServiceCoveragefalseReject a date on which an active source of a multi-feed City has no service
sourceScopesAll sourcesRoute only on the services of these feed scopes in a multi-feed City
departNowfalseTransit only: leave at the current minute in the City's timezone, rounded up; replaces serviceDate and time. Needs a City with one agency timezone
routingDataModeFrom the inputscheduled or realtime; dataMode is an alias. Never send both
realtimeSnapshot—GTFS-Realtime input; see Realtime and traffic
traffic—Drive traffic observations
wheelchairCity profiletrue requires a wheelchair City, false rejects one
bike—Bicycle preferences; see Walk, drive and bike
flex—Include conditional GTFS Flex service in Route and Matrix; see GTFS Flex
monteCarlo—Departure-window distribution; see Monte Carlo
scenarioIdCollection defaultMember of a scenario collection
diagnosticsnonesummary, profile or trace
includeLimitationsfalseAdd dataset limitations to the Result
id—Caller identifier, echoed by the stream and HTTP
kind—route, matrix, reach, compare, native, info or capabilities; required on stream lines

Access padding and overhead from the City's walking policy apply to boarding access, not to a direct walk. The transfer buffer applies once per change, after the transfer walk and any published minimum; it never delays the first boarding, the final walk or staying aboard. Neither control establishes station accessibility or fare eligibility.

arrivalBufferMinutes reserves time before the deadline while keeping the original earliest departure. The deadline must be at least the reserve, and horizonMinutes must exceed it by at least one minute. Via points, depart-at, Walk, Drive, Reach and native operations reject a positive reserve. diagnostics.timeReserves in the trace records both deadlines and calibratedProbability: false. See Time reserves.

Route requests

9 min readSource

On this page

Reference fixtureArrive byWalk, drive and bikeDirect walkingGeometry and faresAlternative journeysShow direct services next to faster journeysShared-leg servicesVia pointsJourney windowsSupported window choicesJourney policyWheelchair and Flex

Route finds a journey between an origin and a destination. A valid request with no journey returns status: "not_found" and exits 0.

Reference fixture

The examples on this page use VIGO's small public test network A → X → B, with service on 2026-07-15. They are executed against the engine on every documentation check. The IDs do not exist in other Cities; the quickstart has a complete Boston walkthrough.

A depart-at request that requires a ride:

JSON
{
  "origin": {"stopId": "A"},
  "destination": {"stopId": "B"},
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "time": "07:55",
  "maxWalkKm": 0.2,
  "requireTransitRide": true
}

The Result, with legs and metadata omitted:

JSON
{
  "schema": "vigo.route.v1",
  "status": "ok",
  "mode": "transit",
  "journey": {
    "departureTime": "07:55:00",
    "arrivalTime": "08:30:00",
    "durationSeconds": 2100,
    "transfers": 1,
    "walkingSeconds": 0,
    "ridingSeconds": 1500,
    "waitingSeconds": 600
  }
}

The journey leaves at 07:55 and arrives at 08:30: 25 minutes riding and 10 minutes waiting. transfers: 1 means two boardings. The public results reference explains every field.

Arrive by

Set timePreference: "arrive_by"; time becomes the deadline. VIGO finds the latest departure that still arrives by then:

JSON
{
  "origin": {"stopId": "A"},
  "destination": {"stopId": "B"},
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "time": "08:30",
  "timePreference": "arrive_by",
  "maxWalkKm": 0.2,
  "maxTransfers": 1,
  "requireTransitRide": true,
  "allowStreetTransfers": false,
  "minimumTransferBufferMinutes": 5
}

Walk, drive and bike

Street modes need coordinates, a clock and a distance limit:

JSON
{
  "origin": {"coordinate": [-77.05, 38.9]},
  "destination": {"coordinate": [-77.03, 38.91]},
  "time": "07:55",
  "mode": "walk",
  "walkSpeedKph": 4.8,
  "maxStreetKm": 5
}

Change mode to drive to drive. A drive attaches each free point to the nearest point of a drivable road and enters or leaves that road mid-segment, in the road's direction. The straight gap is a walk at walkSpeedKph, returned as its own walk leg with geometrySource: "coordinate-snap". When that walk would exceed maxWalkKm, the Result is not_found with reason no_drivable_road_within_walk; VIGO never drives across open ground.

Bike needs a City built with bicycle streets. The bike object sets preferences:

FieldDefaultMeaning
bike.profilebalancedbalanced, quiet or fast. Preferences choose the route; they never inflate the reported duration
bike.speedKph185–40; cycling speed on flat, smooth road. Surface and mapped incline adjust it
bike.maxLtsNo limit1–4; maximum estimated traffic stress. Above it, the rider pushes at 4 km/h where walking is permitted

See Bicycle routing for what the bicycle model includes.

Direct walking

For transit requests between coordinates, a direct walk competes with transit and wins when it arrives sooner. Set requireTransitRide: true to require a boarding, or mode: "walk" to ask for walking. A blocked request that names a stop gains no direct-walk fallback. A direct walk is limited by maxStreetKm, or by maxWalkKm when allowLongWalk is false.

Geometry and fares

Route returns leg geometry by default; includeGeometry: false omits it. A transit leg's line runs from the boarding stop along the aligned GTFS shape to the alighting stop, and its distanceMeters is that line's length. Without a usable shape, the line joins the stop coordinates and says so. Transit legs carry the published GTFS fare for a new boarding when the City has fare data; see Published fares.

Alternative journeys

alternatives (0–9, default 0) asks a depart-at transit Route for more journeys at the requested time. The primary journey stays in journey; the others are in alternatives, earliest arrival first.

alternativeRanking chooses them:

  • pareto (default) keeps trade-offs. Each alternative must beat every other returned journey on arrival, boardings or walking, using no more boardings than the primary journey. When more trade-offs exist than requested, the fewest boardings and the least walking go first. Remaining places go to journeys within the arrival slack that ride a set of routes no listed journey rides, earliest first.
  • ranked keeps the earliest distinct arrivals, even when another journey is better in every respect, then prefers less walking and fewer boardings. A candidate with the same arrival and less walking replaces the primary journey. It allows one more boarding than the primary journey, within maxTransfers.

Journeys on one vehicle chain are one choice in both rankings. alternativeSlackMinutes (0–120, default 15) bounds how much later than the primary journey an alternative may arrive. alternativeSearch in the Result records the coverage, ranking, limits and status. If a search exceeds its label budget, status is unavailable with a reason, and the primary journey is returned alone. Alternatives cannot be combined with arrive-by, via points or a journey window, except a window with windowChoices: "supported".

JSON
{
  "origin": {"stopId": "A"},
  "destination": {"stopId": "B"},
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "time": "07:50",
  "alternatives": 3,
  "alternativeRanking": "ranked",
  "maxWalkKm": 0.2,
  "requireTransitRide": true
}

Show direct services next to faster journeys

Faster journeys with changes can fill every alternative slot before a slower direct service appears. To offer both, send alternatives: 9 with alternativeRanking: "ranked", and a second request with the same endpoints, date, time and walking limits plus maxTransfers: 0. Merge the successful journeys, sort by arrival, remove equivalent departures, and keep the fastest as the recommendation. This is still bounded by the requested count and slack; it is not a list of every service.

Shared-leg services

sharedLegs (default false) on a transit Route lists other services that could replace one leg of the recommended journey. The Result's journey.sharedLegAlternatives.options holds, for each option, a zero-based legIndex and a complete journey. The recommended journey is unchanged.

Services match by route ID, the exact ordered stops with their boarding and alighting permissions, and an equivalent directed path from GTFS shapes or planned geometry (coordinates rounded to six decimals). Route names do not establish identity. A short-turn branch appears only on the part it serves. Missing or mismatched shapes are left out.

Coverage is single_leg_substitutions: each option changes one leg, keeps the other rides, and preserves transfer times and the deadline. Departures are considered from the original leg's departure to 30 minutes later, arriving at most 30 minutes after it. VIGO returns the earliest feasible trip per alternate route, keeps at most 256 candidates per leg and 32 options per journey, and sets truncated: true when a bound is reached. If a substitution VIGO found cannot be rebuilt from the journey's endpoint evidence, it is left out and counted in omitted: {count, reason} (reason access_evidence_unavailable); the next departure of that route is still considered. omitted is absent when nothing was left out, and the recommended journey is unaffected either way. Do not combine options into a journey VIGO has not verified.

The same object reports frequency: "active_departures" and a frequencies entry per verified leg. Each entry counts active trips on the same stops, permissions and path within a half-open window from the leg's departure to 30 minutes later (or the timetable horizon, if earlier). departureCount counts vehicles; uniqueDepartureCount and the sorted departureSeconds count distinct times; departuresPerHour scales the count to an hour; meanHeadwaySeconds, minHeadwaySeconds and maxHeadwaySeconds describe the gaps between distinct times and are null with fewer than two. The scan examines at most 512 departures per leg; when capped, status is incomplete, counts are lower bounds and rates are null. Frequencies describe the segment, not onward connections.

Shared legs work with scheduled and realtime timetables, arrive-by and journey windows. Via points and street modes are rejected.

JSON
{
  "origin": {"stopId": "A"},
  "destination": {"stopId": "B"},
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "time": "07:50",
  "sharedLegs": true,
  "requireTransitRide": true
}

Via points

via (alias waypoints; never both) lists up to 16 intermediate points in order. Each segment is routed in turn, carrying the clock forward for depart-at or backward for arrive-by. No dwell is added at a via point. A blocked segment returns reason via_leg_blocked with its legIndex.

JSON
{
  "origin": {"stopId": "A"},
  "destination": {"stopId": "B"},
  "via": [{"stopId": "X"}],
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "time": "07:55",
  "maxWalkKm": 0.2
}

Transit via requests require a boarding on every segment. They reject maxTransfers and a nonzero transfer buffer, because composing segments cannot certify the change at the via point.

Journey windows

windowMinutes (0–240, default 0) repeats the search every windowStepMinutes (1–60, default 1) from the requested time: depart-at moves to later departures, arrive-by to earlier deadlines. Up to five distinct, nondominated journeys are kept, ordered by arrival (depart-at) or departure (arrive-by), then boardings and walking. The first is in journey; the rest are in alternatives. alternativeSearch records minutes, stepMinutes, searches and direction.

A window samples whole minutes; it is not a continuous profile of every departure. Via points take precedence and remove window sampling from their segments.

JSON
{
  "origin": {"stopId": "A"},
  "destination": {"stopId": "B"},
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "time": "07:50",
  "windowMinutes": 15,
  "windowStepMinutes": 1,
  "maxWalkKm": 0.2,
  "requireTransitRide": true
}

Supported window choices

windowChoices: "supported" asks a depart-at window for the choices a person compares instead of the sampled frontier. VIGO searches each minute of the window and keeps the journeys that are best for some balance of elapsed time, ride time, boardings and walking: the earliest arrival, the fewest transfers, the least walking and a balanced choice, each labeled with its role. With alternatives, alternatives at the requested time join the choices.

FieldMeaning
expandedWalkKm0.2–5, above maxWalkKm: also search with this walking budget and add choices that walk farther but arrive at least one minute earlier than every ordinary choice. They carry expandedWalkingLimitKm
includeEarliestTransitAdd earliestTransit: the first boarding and arrival of the earliest transit choice, even when walking wins

With via points, each segment starts at the exact clock the previous one reaches its point. Arrive-by accepts windowChoices only without a window.

The compiler, vigo-build, offers a different window: departureWindowMinutes (or --departure-window), a centered depart-at profile of ±0–30 minutes. It rejects the engine's window fields.

Journey policy

journeyPolicy set to "alternatives-v1" on a transit Route returns the journey and its alternatives as one versioned policy for thin clients. Check that capabilities.route.journeyPolicies lists it. The policy keeps a direct transit journey and a permitted direct walk, orders by arrival (departure for arrive-by), then walking and boardings, and bundles journeys that share boarding and alighting stations, modes and walking policy. Arrive-by keeps a 15-minute window of earlier arrivals, sampled every five minutes. Do not combine it with alternatives, windows or via points.

expandedWalkKm is explicit permission to search with more walking; omit it when the user's walking limit is binding. A wider choice must beat every ordinary choice by at least one minute. In supported windows, a final ride (with its wait) is replaced by walking on when the walk fits the wider budget and arrives at least a minute sooner. requireTransitRide excludes walking-only choices. A failed wider search keeps the ordinary results.

Wheelchair and Flex

A City built with --wheelchair answers with the strict wheelchair-strict-v1 profile; wheelchair: true requires such a City and false rejects it. Wheelchair Cities reject Drive, realtime transit and query-time scenario overlays. See Wheelchair routing.

flex: {} on Route or Matrix includes conditional GTFS Flex service. Optional durationFactor (1–10) and durationOffsetSeconds (0–7200) apply when the feed omits its own safe-duration values; bookingConfirmed: true records the caller's claim. See GTFS Flex.

Reference

Matrix requests

1 min readSource

On this page

Build a matrixRead the matrixJourneys and journey formatRepeated endpoints

Matrix returns travel times between every origin and destination in one request, for transit, walking, driving or cycling.

Build a matrix

Supply origins and destinations, each at least one point. Rows follow origins and columns follow destinations. A request holds up to 65,536 pairs.

JSON
{
  "origins": [{"stopId": "A"}, {"stopId": "X"}],
  "destinations": [{"stopId": "B"}, {"stopId": "A"}],
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "time": "07:55",
  "maxWalkKm": 0.2,
  "requireTransitRide": true,
  "includeJourneys": true,
  "includeGeometry": true
}

Read the matrix

durationsSeconds[row][column] is the time from the shared departure to arrival (depart-at), or from the latest departure to the shared deadline (arrive-by). An arrive-by duration can exceed its journey's duration when the journey arrives early. null means unreachable; zero is a real zero-length trip. Walk, Drive and Bike matrices also return distancesMeters in the same order.

Journeys and journey format

FieldDefaultMeaning
includeJourneysfalseTransit only. Adds journeys[row][column], with null for unreachable pairs
includeGeometryfalseRequires journeys. Adds leg geometry
journeyFormatfullcompact returns the same trips, stops, boarding sequences, clocks and totals without display metadata or walking evidence. Requires journeys; excludes geometry

When a direct walk wins a transit cell, its journey has one timed walking leg. Large journey matrices with geometry can reach the response limit; split them. Output detail never changes the search.

Repeated endpoints

Repeated origins or destinations are searched once and expanded back to the requested rows and columns. Stops and coordinates keep their own semantics: two co-located stops are not merged. The trace reports matrixReuse with requestedPairs, searchPairs, uniqueOrigins and uniqueDestinations.

Reach requests

5 min readSource

On this page

Depart atArrive byOptionsSurface samplingRead the surfaceMap outputStreet evidenceAll-day Reach

Reach maps where an origin can reach within time cutoffs, or, arriving by a deadline, where a destination can be reached from. isochrone is an alias. Transit Reach combines the timetable with walking on the prepared streets; mode can also be walk, drive or bike.

Depart at

JSON
{
  "origin": {"stopId": "A"},
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "time": "07:55",
  "cutoffsMinutes": [15, 30, 45],
  "maxWalkKm": 0.5,
  "walkSpeedKph": 4.8,
  "extentRadiusKm": 2,
  "rasterSize": 48,
  "includeStreetEdges": true
}

Arrive by

Arrive-by Reach takes a destination instead of an origin and reads time as the deadline. Each value is how long before the deadline a traveler must leave that place, including any wait after an early arrival; a stop's value is how long before the deadline the traveler must be at the stop.

JSON
{
  "destination": {"stopId": "B"},
  "timePreference": "arrive_by",
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "time": "08:30",
  "cutoffsMinutes": [15, 30, 45],
  "maxWalkKm": 0.5,
  "extentRadiusKm": 2,
  "rasterSize": 48
}

Transit searches the timetable backward once, giving every stop its latest boarding. Walking runs backward over directed streets, so one-way paths, escalators and station paths keep their direction. A destination behind authorized private access is entered from its public exits. A deadline earlier than the longest cutoff after midnight searches the previous service day's late trips. Scenario exclusions and planned services apply; a compiled overlay and surfaceReuse are depart-at only.

Options

FieldDefaultMeaning
originRequired for depart-atWhere trips start
destinationRequired for arrive-byWhere trips end
cutoffsMinutes[15, 30, 45, 60]1–16 values, each 1–240; sorted and deduplicated
rasterSize96Integer 16–1024; cells per side
extentRadiusKm81–40; the grid's extent around the point, not a trip-distance limit
boundsFrom the point and radius[west, south, east, north]; fixes the grid explicitly
surfaceSamplingstreetstreet samples reached street intervals; cell-center routes to every cell center
reachFormatfullfull, map (areas only) or surface (no polygons or contours)
includeStreetEdgesfalseAdd directed street evidence (full only)
includeNodesfalseAdd reached-node evidence, up to 30,000 nodes (full only)
scenario—Exclusions, planned services or a compiled overlay
surfaceReuse—Street sampling: baseline keeps this surface in the running process; a following scenario request grows from it when every seed is unchanged or earlier
allDay—Aggregate depart-at samples over a window; see All-day Reach
arrayEncodingjsonbase64 encodes rasters and street evidence as little-endian arrays; detailed stream output only

Reach rejects horizonMinutes, maxStreetKm, requireTransitRide and allowLongWalk: the largest cutoff bounds the search. Walk-only Reach needs no service date and cannot take a transit scenario.

Drive and Bike Reach route from the point to every cell center, with a 750 km road-distance cap, and return no pedestrian street evidence. The point and each cell center walk straight to their nearest road, and that walk counts toward the cutoff. Dated Bike Reach evaluates timed roads and turns; its cutoffs filter the preferred route's elapsed time.

Surface sampling

street (default) records the earliest reached part of each street in each cell; cells away from reached streets stay empty, and a filled cell does not establish a route to its center. It supports planned service and any walking speed.

cell-center routes to the center of every cell with the Matrix walking rules and the requested bounds. It supports walking and scheduled transit without planned service, and transit uses the City's 4.8 km/h walking policy; other speeds are rejected. Use it to compare with tools that evaluate grid points.

Read the surface

surface.valuesSeconds is a flat, row-major array of seconds starting at the northwest cell: cell (x, y) is index y * width + x. null means no value was reached; zero is a value. With bounds [west, south, east, north], the center of a cell is:

longitude = west + (x + 0.5) / width  * (east - west)
latitude  = north - (y + 0.5) / height * (north - south)

fullSurface uses the same dimensions over bounds recomputed from the reached streets, which can be smaller or larger than the requested view; never read its values with the requested bounds. areas and fullAreas are GeoJSON FeatureCollections of MultiPolygons, and contours and fullContours of MultiLineStrings; each feature carries its cutoff. Areas keep holes and separate islands; contours interpolate the raster and never draw a hull across unreachable space.

Map output

reachFormat: "map" returns only the full reached-area polygons as areas, their bounds, and the usual metadata: no raster, stops or contours. The polygons equal fullAreas from the default full format. Map output cannot be compared; use full for analysis.

Street evidence

includeStreetEdges: true (or --street-edges) adds surface.edges with schemaVersion: "vigo.standalone.street-edges.v2" and encoding: "indexed-json": the directed street intervals reached, with times and walking distances. Decode directed street evidence shows how to read them.

All-day Reach

allDay samples scheduled depart-at transit every five minutes over a service-day window, default [0, 1440) minutes (288 samples). Omit time and timeMinutes.

JSON
{
  "kind": "reach",
  "origin": {"stopId": "B"},
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "allDay": {"startMinutes": 0, "endMinutes": 1440},
  "cutoffsMinutes": [15, 30, 45],
  "maxWalkKm": 0.5,
  "rasterSize": 48,
  "extentRadiusKm": 2,
  "reachFormat": "surface"
}

Run it with vigo reach or on a stream line. It supports street sampling, scheduled transit, depart-at and reachFormat: "surface" only; scenarios, realtime, arrive-by, cell-center sampling, polygons, caching switches, node and edge evidence and per-sample output are rejected. Studio and the compiler do not offer it.

The Result keeps schema: "vigo.reach.v1". allDay.sampleCount is the denominator. The surface holds reachableSamples, meanReachableDurationSeconds (null when never reached) and reachableSamplesByCutoff, one row per entry of cutoffsSeconds. Divide a count by the sample count for the share of departures that reach the cell. The mean covers only the reachable samples, so a low mean does not mean reliable access. Memory does not grow with the number of samples.
