Scenario requests

5 min readSource

On this page

Route on a scenarioScenario fieldsFrequency servicePreserve explicit departures and dwellCompiled overlays

A scenario changes the transit service seen by one Reach or transit Route request. It changes nothing in the City or in later requests. See Scenarios for how to design one.

Route on a scenario

A Route scenario routes on the scheduled timetable with excluded trips removed and planned services added. Planned stops given as stopId are those stops; others are new stops, joined to the network by walks within the City's stop-transfer radius and reachable within maxWalkKm. Planned stops, routes and trips belong to the feed scenario-<hash>; a planned route's ID is its service id and its name is the service name. Route scenarios accept services and exclusions, not overlay, and use scheduled data. Repeating a scenario reuses its timetable view.

JSON
{
  "origin": {"stopId": "A"},
  "destination": {"stopId": "B"},
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "time": "07:55",
  "maxWalkKm": 0.2,
  "requireTransitRide": true,
  "scenario": {
    "id": "express",
    "name": "Express",
    "services": [{
      "id": "express",
      "name": "Express",
      "operation": "add",
      "scheduleMode": "frequency",
      "stops": [{"stopId": "A"}, {"stopId": "B"}],
      "bidirectional": false,
      "startMinutes": 475,
      "endMinutes": 600,
      "headwayMinutes": 5,
      "timeModel": "preserve-scheduled",
      "segmentRuntimeMinutes": [5]
    }]
  }
}

Scenario fields

FieldMeaning
id, nameLabels, echoed in Results
cityRevisionOptional; must equal the loaded City's revision
excludedTripIds, excludedRouteIdsExact active IDs to remove; exclusions affect matching scheduled trips only
servicesUp to 128 planned services
overlayA compiled overlay instead of services (Reach only)
flexZonesPlanned on-demand zones for Route and transit Reach; see GTFS Flex

Send either nonempty services or overlay. Editor-only fields are rejected: convert branch edits into explicit schedules first.

Frequency service

JSON
{
  "origin": {"stopId": "A"},
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "time": "07:55",
  "cutoffsMinutes": [15, 30, 45],
  "extentRadiusKm": 2,
  "rasterSize": 48,
  "maxWalkKm": 0.2,
  "scenario": {
    "services": [{
      "id": "express",
      "operation": "add",
      "scheduleMode": "frequency",
      "stops": [{"stopId": "A"}, {"stopId": "B"}],
      "bidirectional": false,
      "startMinutes": 475,
      "endMinutes": 600,
      "headwayMinutes": 5,
      "timeModel": "preserve-scheduled",
      "segmentRuntimeMinutes": [5]
    }]
  }
}
Service fieldDefaultMeaning
operationaddadd, augment or replace
stopsRequiredAt least two points in service order; at most 256 distinct planned points per request
scheduleModefrequency (add, augment); preserve-trips (replace)How departures are made
sourceRouteId—Route replaced by a frequency replace without explicit trips
bidirectionaltrue for frequencyAlso run the reverse direction. Preserved trips reject true
startMinutes, endMinutes300, 15000–4319; end after start. The window includes its end unless exactTimes is true
headwayMinutes120.1–1440
exactTimes—true fixes departures at the start and every headway, excluding the end; otherwise Monte Carlo samples a phase
timeModelestimate-distanceestimate-distance, preserve-scheduled or infer-road
averageSpeedKph221–300; with distance estimates
dwellMinutes0.350–60; dwell after arriving at each intermediate stop
segmentRuntimeMinutes—One value per consecutive stop pair
segmentDistancesKm—One value per consecutive stop pair
addedStopDwellMinutes00–10; dwell at inserted stops with supplied runtimes
scheduledTrips—Explicit trips for preserve-trips
timetables—Up to 32 timetable rows replacing the top-level window; see Monte Carlo
phaseFrom—Coordinate a non-exact service with another; Monte Carlo only
timing—Speed and dwell edits for preserve-trips; see Monte Carlo

A request accepts at most one million planned stop events. estimate-distance uses the projected distance between stops, the speed and the dwell; supplying runtimes does not select them. preserve-scheduled uses supplied runtimes, falling back to distance estimates. infer-road consumes supplied distances or runtimes; the engine does not trace roads itself.

Frequency windows use whole seconds. Every run arrives, dwells, then departs, so riders alight before the dwell; runs do not dwell at their first or last stop. A frequency service runs on every service day: the previous day's runs still running after midnight and the next day's first runs join the timetable wherever the query's clock reaches them, and no departure runs twice.

augment keeps existing service. A frequency replace with sourceRouteId removes the route's active trips; with scheduledTrips, their trip IDs define what is removed. Added service can run on a date with no baseline service.

Preserve explicit departures and dwell

JSON
{
  "origin": {"stopId": "A"},
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
  "time": "07:55",
  "cutoffsMinutes": [30, 45],
  "extentRadiusKm": 2,
  "rasterSize": 48,
  "maxWalkKm": 0.2,
  "scenario": {
    "services": [{
      "operation": "replace",
      "scheduleMode": "preserve-trips",
      "stops": [{"stopId": "X"}, {"stopId": "B"}],
      "scheduledTrips": [{
        "tripId": "T2",
        "departureSeconds": 29700,
        "arrivalOffsetsSeconds": [0, 600],
        "departureOffsetsSeconds": [0, 600],
        "canBoard": [1, 0],
        "canAlight": [0, 1]
      }]
    }]
  }
}

Offsets are seconds after the run's departureSeconds, one per stop, in chronological order. canBoard and canAlight are 0 or 1 per stop and default to all allowed. Unknown trip fields are rejected. The replaced tripId must be active on its service day. serviceDayOffset (−3 to 3, default 0) names the service day a trip runs on: a trip with −1 belongs to the previous day, its departureSeconds are on that day's clock, and only its calls after the query date's midnight remain. A replacement removes every instance of its original trip, so include the previous day's trips that run past midnight; Studio and the compiler do. Preserved trips never create reverse runs.

Compiled overlays

Advanced clients can send scenario.overlay with the arrays of TimetableOverlayManyQueryInput: stops, overlayStopCount, direction offsets, stops and times, service windows and headways, and supplemental transfers. The stop count must match the coordinate-bearing stop list and be at most 256. Direction stops use overlay-local indices; supplemental transfers use the combined resident-plus-overlay domain. The native field reference gives the exact types.

Compare requests

1 min readSource

On this page

Prepare the comparisonInterpret changes

compare reports where travel times improve, worsen, appear or disappear between two saved Reach Results on the same grid.

Prepare the comparison

Send the two complete Result objects under before and after; not filenames:

Shell
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
with open('baseline.json') as f:
    before = json.load(f)
with open('scenario.json') as f:
    after = json.load(f)
with open('comparison.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump({'before': before, 'after': after}, f)
PY
vigo compare --city ./city --request comparison.json --output change.json

Python is only a convenient way to build the file. The engine requires a City path for compare even though it does not route. Both Results must share the City revision, bounds, dimensions and compatible rasters. Engine Compare accepts Reach only; the compiler's vigo-build compare --before … --after … also compares Route and Matrix Results.

Interpret changes

The Result, vigo.compare.v1, reports after minus before. counts splits the cells reachable in both (comparable) into faster, slower and unchanged, and counts newlyReachable and noLongerReachable separately. meanChangeSeconds averages comparable cells, is negative when travel got faster, and is null when none are comparable. The trace has the per-cell deltaMinutes grid; see Comparison output.

Compare checks the grid, not the experiment: keep the origin, date, clock, walking policy and cutoffs identical yourself.

Scenario collections

1 min readSource

A collection serves several transit scenarios over one immutable street graph. Build it from a source manifest, then serve or stream it:

Shell
vigo build-scenarios --spec scenarios.source.json --output ./scenario-set
vigo serve --city ./scenario-set --port 8080
JSON
{
  "schemaVersion": "vigo.scenarios.source.v1",
  "name": "Regional alternatives",
  "osm": { "path": "region.osm.pbf" },
  "streetModes": "walk",
  "prepareDates": ["2026-10-05"],
  "defaultScenario": "baseline",
  "maximumResidentScenarios": 2,
  "scenarios": [
    { "id": "baseline", "name": "Baseline", "feeds": [{ "path": "baseline.zip", "scope": "agency" }] },
    { "id": "proposal", "name": "Proposal", "feeds": [{ "path": "proposal.zip", "scope": "agency" }] }
  ]
}

Source paths are relative to the manifest; optional sha256 values pin each input. Streets are prepared once and referenced from every member, so move the collection as one directory. build-scenarios takes --spec, --output, --wheelchair and --wheelchair-streets, prints the same progress as build for each member, and prints the collection manifest with its storageBytes on standard output. The output directory holds scenarios.json, checksums.json (a SHA-256 for every file), cities/<id> and streets/<OSM SHA-256>. It must not exist yet; the collection is staged beside it and renamed into place when complete, and an interrupted build is removed as for build. prepareDates precompiles up to 32 service dates; other dates still work from the source timetable.

Each request selects a member with scenarioId (or --scenario); omission selects defaultScenario. At most maximumResidentScenarios members stay loaded; see Runtime memory and caching.

  • "privateAccess": "endpoints" gives every member the authorized endpoint access overlay. These members keep separate street directories, because the overlay depends on each member's stops.
  • "wheelchair": true (or build-scenarios --wheelchair) prepares every member with wheelchair-strict-v1. Wheelchair collections require streetModes: "walk" and public access. Conflicting command-line and manifest values are rejected.

Reference

Realtime and traffic input

8 min readSource

On this page

Transit snapshotService AlertsAutomatic GTFS-RT pollingDrive trafficAutomatic NDW pollingImport NDW DATEX II v3 traffic

A query can carry GTFS-Realtime predictions or traffic observations, and vigo serve can poll feeds itself. Without polling, each query uses only what it carries; the next request without it is scheduled again.

routingDataMode: "scheduled" rejects observation input; "realtime" requires a snapshot, traffic or a polling server. Without an explicit mode, supplied input selects its path.

Transit snapshot

Transit Route, Matrix and Reach accept realtimeSnapshot and all search the same realtime timetable; a Reach scenario applies on top of it. Send a FULL_DATASET snapshot with tripUpdates and, optionally, alerts. Timestamps are POSIX seconds. Every record needs a sourceFeedTimestamp or the snapshot's feedTimestamp, at most 180 seconds old and at most 60 seconds ahead; a record's own timestamp, when present, must also be fresh.

To try it on the fixture, add a current synthetic delay to the first route request:

Shell
python3 - <<'PY'
import json, time
with open('route.json') as f:
    query = json.load(f)
query['routingDataMode'] = 'realtime'
query['realtimeSnapshot'] = {
    'incrementality': 'FULL_DATASET',
    'feedTimestamp': int(time.time()),
    'tripUpdates': [{'tripId': 'T2', 'delaySeconds': 600}]
}
with open('realtime-route.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(query, f)
PY
vigo route --city ./city --request realtime-route.json

In real use, keep the provider's timestamps. Rewriting them to look current changes the input; it does not replay the observation.

Trip update fieldMeaning
tripIdExact, or unambiguous scoped or local, static trip ID; nested trip.tripId is also accepted
sourceScopeThe feed scope the record belongs to in a multi-feed City; omit it in a single-feed City
startDateOptional service date check (YYYYMMDD or YYYY-MM-DD)
routeId, directionIdOptional identity checks
delaySecondsTrip delay, propagated forward
scheduleRelationshipSCHEDULED, CANCELED, DELETED or REPLACEMENT
stopTimeUpdatesPredictions for individual calls

A stop time update names its call by stopSequence or an unambiguous stopId; when both are present they must agree, and loops need the sequence. arrival and departure are separate objects with an integer delay or an absolute time in seconds. Absolute times need realtimeSnapshot.timezone when the City has more than one timezone. SKIPPED removes a call; NO_DATA resets the propagated delay. A REPLACEMENT must give every call with an existing stop, an increasing sequence and absolute times.

Invalid, duplicate, stale, ambiguous and unmatched records keep scheduled service and are counted. A malformed snapshot fails the request. meta.realtime reports coverage and the counts of applied, canceled, stale, invalid, duplicate and unmatched records; Realtime transit explains how to read them. A transit leg on an updated trip reports quality.schedule: "realtime".

Service Alerts

realtimeSnapshot.alerts holds Service Alerts, in the form the server's poller produces:

JSON
{
  "id": "closure-1",
  "effect": "NO_SERVICE",
  "header": "Park Street closed",
  "activePeriods": [{ "start": 1792764000, "end": 1792778400 }],
  "informedEntities": [{ "stopId": "place-pktrm" }, { "routeId": "Red", "directionId": 0 }]
}

An informed entity matches when all of its fields match (routeId, routeType, directionId, trip.tripId, stopId); an alert applies when any entity matches. A station stopId also selects its platforms. Active periods are POSIX seconds with open bounds; no period means always active. effect is a name or its GTFS-Realtime code.

EffectRouting
NO_SERVICE on a route, trip or route typeIts trips cannot be boarded or left during the period
NO_SERVICE on a stopNo boarding or alighting there; vehicles pass through
NO_SERVICE on a route and a stopThat route does not serve that stop
Any other effectNone; the alert is reported on the legs it describes

Every fresh alert active during a ride that selects its trip, route or stops appears in the leg's alerts (id, effect, cause, severity, header, description, url). meta.realtime.alerts counts received, fresh, stale and NO_SERVICE alerts, the closed boardings and alightings, and entities VIGO cannot resolve, such as an agency alone or a direction without a route. A City with several timezones reports status: "timezone_required" unless the snapshot has a timezone. Wheelchair Cities use scheduled service, so ACCESSIBILITY_ISSUE is reported, not applied.

Automatic GTFS-RT polling

Shell
vigo serve --city ./city --realtime-poll ./realtime.json
JSON
{
  "sources": [
    { "url": "https://cdn.mbta.com/realtime/TripUpdates.pb", "kind": "tripUpdates", "sourceScope": "mbta" },
    { "url": "https://cdn.mbta.com/realtime/Alerts.pb", "kind": "alerts", "sourceScope": "mbta" }
  ],
  "intervalSeconds": 30,
  "timeoutSeconds": 10
}
FieldMeaning
sources[].urlHTTPS, or loopback HTTP for local mirrors. Redirects are rejected
sources[].kindfeed (default: Trip Updates and Alerts), tripUpdates or alerts. Vehicle Positions are never polled
sources[].sourceScopeThe static feed the source describes, in a multi-feed City
sources[].headersUp to eight request headers, such as an API key. Status output never shows URLs, queries or headers
intervalSeconds5–3600
timeoutSeconds1–60 per request

Up to 16 sources. Downloads are limited to 32 MiB, or 128 MiB after gzip, and each feed must be a FULL_DATASET FeedMessage within the snapshot limits.

Set routingDataMode: "realtime" and omit realtimeSnapshot to route on the server's latest snapshot; an inline snapshot takes precedence for its own query. meta.realtime.snapshot names the snapshot used (source: "server", its id, generation, and each source's timestamp and failure). Identical content never publishes a new generation.

One background producer downloads, decodes and merges the sources; routing never waits for a download. While idle, the worker installs each publication and derives the realtime view of the last live query, so the next one normally finds it ready. A failed source keeps its last good records without extending their validity: they still expire after 180 seconds, and coverage.complete becomes false. Failures back off exponentially, up to one hour. GET /v1/realtime reports status (fresh, stale_fallback or unavailable_fallback), generation, snapshot ID, counts, attempts, failures, the next attempt and each source's state.

Polling serves a single City, not a scenario collection. DIFFERENTIAL feeds, deleted entities, added trips and trip modifications are not applied.

Drive traffic

Drive Route and Matrix accept a traffic object. With routingDataMode: "realtime", it replaces the road costs for that request: one fixed set of costs, not a forecast that changes during the trip.

FieldMeaning
observedAtObservation time, RFC 3339 or Unix seconds or milliseconds; aliases fetchedAt, timestamp. Required
ttlSecondsValidity, 1–1800; default 300
expiresAtOptional explicit expiry
sourceProvider label
observationsThe observed roads; aliases segments, edgeUpdates

At now >= expiresAt the request uses baseline costs and reports stale_fallback. Observation times more than 60 seconds in the future and malformed validity are rejected. The admission clock is fixed once per request.

Each observation identifies a directed road by coordinates (2–512 points), by fromCoordinate and toCoordinate, or by edgeIndices bound to the City's streetSourceFingerprint, and sets exactly one effect:

EffectRange
closed: trueMakes the matched directed edges unavailable
travelTimeSeconds0.01–86400 for the whole matched path, spread in proportion to baseline edge times
speedKph1–200
delayFactor1–100; aliases factor and multiplier

At most 100,000 observations and 200,000 affected edges. Geometry is matched to a connected directed path: the matcher checks endpoint proximity, forward progress, shape coverage within a corridor at most 30 m wide, and length, and rejects competing paths within its ambiguity margin. Opposite directions are separate. Unmatched, ambiguous and over-budget observations are reported, never guessed. Overlapping observations keep the largest cost, and no edge becomes faster than baseline.

Raw callers can send snapshotKey, edgeIndices and edgeTimeUnits (hundredths of a second; 2147483647 closes an edge) with the streetSourceFingerprint. The actual weights, not the key, decide cache identity. meta.traffic reports status, timestamps, the effective key, matching counts and rejections.

Automatic NDW polling

Shell
vigo serve --city ./city --ndw-poll ./ndw.json
JSON
{
  "configurationUrl": "https://opendata.ndw.nu/reistijden_configuratie_meetlocaties.xml.gz",
  "measurementsUrl": "https://opendata.ndw.nu/reistijden_meetgegevens.xml.gz",
  "intervalSeconds": 60,
  "configurationRefreshSeconds": 3600,
  "ttlSeconds": 300,
  "timeoutSeconds": 20
}

Every field is optional; {} selects these defaults. URLs require HTTPS, except loopback HTTP; redirects are rejected. Ranges: intervalSeconds 1–3600, configurationRefreshSeconds 60–86400, ttlSeconds 1–1800, timeoutSeconds 1–60. Poll at the source's update cadence, normally 60 seconds. Downloads are limited to 16 MiB and decompressed XML to 256 MiB.

Set routingDataMode: "realtime" and omit traffic to drive on the latest snapshot; an inline traffic takes precedence. Before the first successful poll, realtime Drive reports meta.traffic.status: "unavailable_fallback"; after expiry, stale_fallback. Both use baseline costs.

One background producer downloads, joins and matches the feed to the City's driving graph. Only sites whose endpoints lie within 120 m of the City bounds are kept. Failures keep the last snapshot without extending its validity and back off up to one hour. GET /v1/traffic reports freshness, generation, attempts, failures, the next retry, matching counts and timings. Polling serves a single City, not a collection, and never rewrites City files. A new metric still needs one customization of the driving hierarchy on its first query.

Import NDW DATEX II v3 traffic

traffic-import converts local NDW files into a traffic object:

Shell
vigo traffic-import --city ./city \
  --configuration reistijden_configuratie_meetlocaties.xml.gz \
  --measurements reistijden_meetgegevens.xml.gz \
  --ttl-seconds 300 --output traffic.json

Download both publications from the NDW open-data portal. Put the output in a request's traffic field with routingDataMode: "realtime". The City must include driving. Import again for each feed update; a failed import leaves the previous output file unchanged. ingestion in the output reports rejected records, matching results and timings.

The importer targets the Verkeersdata NL DATEX II 3.6 AVG profile. It joins table identity, site identity and version, and measurement index; reads ordered GML geometry; and uses the measurement time, not the publication or download time. Invalid values, forecasts, erroneous measurements and stale records are excluded. The snapshot expires with its earliest retained measurement.

Supported observations are whole-path travel times and speeds with an explicit linear itinerary and unrestricted vehicle scope. Point detectors, lane- or vehicle-class values, OpenLR or ALERT-C locations, incident and closure publications, and time overrides are rejected with reasons. No closure is inferred from a missing or zero measurement. Matching is conservative geometric conflation, not proof that the provider and OpenStreetMap describe the same road; inspect the matched coverage before relying on it.

Resident streaming

1 min readSource

stream keeps a City loaded and answers one JSON request per standard-input line, in order:

NDJSON
{"kind":"route","id":"trip-1","origin":{"stopId":"A"},"destination":{"stopId":"B"},"serviceDate":"2026-07-15","time":"07:55","maxWalkKm":0.2}
{"kind":"reach","id":"area-1","origin":{"stopId":"A"},"serviceDate":"2026-07-15","time":"07:55","cutoffsMinutes":[30],"rasterSize":48,"extentRadiusKm":2}
Shell
vigo stream --city ./city < requests.ndjson > results.ndjson

Every line needs kind: route, matrix, reach (or isochrone), compare, native, info or capabilities. Output is one compact JSON object per line, in input order, echoing id and adding a sequence number. Blank lines are ignored. Each line may use its own service date; a new date replaces the active timetable, and recently used timetables are retained. An invalid line returns a vigo.error.v1 object on standard output and the stream continues; a line over 8 MiB ends the stream. Close standard input to finish.

When the stream opens, it prepares modes in the background as VIGO_PREPARE selects; a first request waits only for the part it needs. The stream has no query deadline or restart; use serve or your own supervisor for those. --stream-output=detailed returns vigo.stream.detail.v1 envelopes holding the internal trace; check that capabilities.output.streamFormats lists detailed first.

Measure a fresh process's first answer separately from later answers in a resident process.

HTTP API

6 min readSource

On this page

EndpointsServer limitsCancel a requestStatus codesAuthenticationClient integrationSend a request

vigo serve answers the same JSON requests over HTTP. The OpenAPI document is served at /openapi.json; the guide, with an API console at the end of this page, is served at /.

Endpoints

Method and pathResponseAuthentication
GET /, /docs, /docs/This guide, offline, with an API consolePublic
GET /openapi.json, /docs/openapi.json, /standalone-openapi.json, /docs/standalone-openapi.jsonOpenAPI 3.1 documentPublic
GET /healthz200 while the process runs; status is ready or recoveringPublic; no City data
GET /readyz200 when a worker is ready, 503 while it recoversPublic; no City data
GET /v1/capabilitiesFeatures of this executableProtected
GET /v1/infoThe loaded City or collectionProtected
GET /v1/realtimeGTFS-RT polling statusProtected
GET /v1/trafficNDW polling statusProtected
POST /v1/routeRouteProtected
POST /v1/matrixMatrixProtected
POST /v1/reach, /v1/isochroneReachProtected
POST /v1/compareCompare two saved Reach ResultsProtected
POST /v1/nativeA native operationProtected
DELETE /v1/requests/{id}Cancel a named requestProtected

"Protected" means a bearer token when VIGO_API_TOKEN is set, and otherwise a loopback Host and same-origin browser requests; see Authentication.

The path selects the query; a body kind is overwritten. Send Content-Type: application/json with a Content-Length or a bounded chunked HTTP/1.1 body. Conflicting length headers are rejected. Each connection closes after its response: there is no keep-alive, HTTP/2, WebSocket, gzip, streamed response or CORS. Every response carries a restrictive Content-Security-Policy that lets the embedded API console call only this service. Query parameters diagnostics (or vigo_diagnostics), includeGeometry and includeLimitations set the matching body fields; conflicting values are rejected.

Server limits

The service runs an HTTP front end and one supervised worker process that keeps the City loaded and answers one query at a time; a query can use several threads. Request bodies are read outside the worker. A worker that times out or fails is stopped and replaced. The service keeps no client sessions.

Server flags set the main limits; see Server flags. Beyond them:

  • Uploads and queued requests share a 64 MiB admission budget, and pending responses a 128 MiB budget. A worker result counts against the response budget while it is read, not after it is buffered, so a large result never exceeds it. Exhaustion returns 503, before 100 Continue for uploads.
  • Headers are limited to 16 KiB and 64 entries. A worker result is limited to 64 MiB; split large matrices or rasters.
  • Writing a response has a 10-second deadline. A worker may take up to 60 seconds to open the City.
  • Waiting routes and matrices of up to 1,024 cells get up to 32 turns or 250 ms of worker time before the oldest waiting analytical request, so a batch of Reach jobs cannot starve point queries. The running query always finishes first.
  • GET /healthz, /readyz, /v1/capabilities, /v1/realtime, /v1/traffic and DELETE /v1/requests/{id} may use four connections beyond --max-connections, so a service saturated by data requests still reports its health and accepts cancellations.
  • A client that closes its connection while its query waits or runs cancels the query, as DELETE /v1/requests/{id} does. A client that half-closes its sending side counts as gone.

One worker answers one query at a time: --max-connections and --max-queue bound waiting work, they do not add parallel computation, and a long Reach or Matrix delays the queries behind it. To serve more queries at once, run several services, each with its own worker and City, behind a load balancer that bounds its own queue, and keep expensive analysis on separate instances when interactive latency matters. Each instance holds its own City in memory. Request IDs are per instance, so send DELETE /v1/requests/{id} to the instance that received the request. Measure throughput with an open-loop load such as scripts/stress-http.py (see Reproduce a service workload).

These limits bound transport buffers, not process memory. See Resource limits.

Cancel a request

Give a request an id of up to 128 letters, digits, hyphens, underscores or periods. DELETE /v1/requests/{id} returns 202, and the original request returns 499. Running work is stopped and its worker replaced; queued work is skipped. Reusing an active ID returns 409. Closing the client connection cancels a query the same way, with or without an id.

Status codes

StatusMeaning
200A Result, including not_found Routes; or metadata and documentation
202Cancellation accepted
400Invalid query, JSON or HTTP framing
401Missing or wrong bearer token
403Without a token: a non-loopback Host, or a browser Origin other than the service's own
404Unknown path or method
408Request read deadline
409The request id is already active
413Body over the limit
417Unsupported Expect header
431Headers too large
499Canceled through DELETE /v1/requests/{id}, or by the client closing its connection
503Connection, queue or buffer capacity exhausted, or worker unavailable; readiness uses it too
504Query deadline, worker failure or response failure

Errors use schema: "vigo.error.v1" with error.code and error.message; handle the code and status, not the message. Retry 503 with backoff. For 504, reduce the work or read the worker log before raising deadlines. A transport error never means a trip is unreachable.

The service logs its address to standard error. If a replacement worker cannot start, the first failure of each streak is logged, /readyz and queries return 503, and restarts back off from 250 ms to 10 seconds.

Authentication

Set VIGO_API_TOKEN to protect every /v1 endpoint, including on loopback, and send Authorization: Bearer <token>. A non-loopback --host requires a token of at least 16 characters. Set it through your secret store: it is never a command-line argument, and the service does not store tokens or request bodies.

Without a token, a loopback service accepts data requests only when Host is 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1] (with an optional port) and any Origin is that same http:// origin; other requests get 403. This blocks DNS rebinding and cross-site requests. A local reverse proxy that sends another Host needs a token. The guide, the OpenAPI document and the health endpoints are always public and contain no City data.

Shell
export VIGO_CITY=/srv/vigo/city
# Set VIGO_API_TOKEN through your shell or platform secret store.
vigo serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
  --query-timeout-ms 30000 --max-queue 8 --max-connections 32

curl --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/route \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIGO_API_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @route.json

Terminate HTTPS at a reverse proxy, and give its upstream timeout room for the query deadline plus transfer. Deploy the routing engine covers containers and process managers.

Client integration

Any HTTP client works; no VIGO package is needed. A Python standard-library client:

Python
import json
import os
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

query = {
    "origin": {"stopId": "A"},
    "destination": {"stopId": "B"},
    "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
    "time": "07:55",
    "maxWalkKm": 0.2,
}
headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
if os.environ.get("VIGO_API_TOKEN"):
    headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + os.environ["VIGO_API_TOKEN"]
request = urllib.request.Request(
    "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/route",
    data=json.dumps(query).encode(), headers=headers,
)
try:
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=45) as response:
        result = json.load(response)
except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
    raise RuntimeError(error.read().decode()) from error
if result["status"] == "not_found":
    print("No journey:", result["reason"]["code"])
else:
    print(result["journey"]["arrivalTime"], len(result["journey"]["legs"]), "legs")

Read the HTTP status before the body: a 200 body can be a valid not_found. Keep bearer tokens on servers; never embed a shared token in public web code. For reproducible work, keep the executable version, capabilities, City revision, complete request, observation timestamps and Result together.

Send a request

Checking for a VIGO service at this address…

Every variable the engine reads. Command-line flags override the matching variables.


VariableDefaultMeaning
VIGO_CITY—Default City or collection path; --city overrides it
PORT8080Default port for serve and health; --port overrides it
VIGO_API_TOKEN—Bearer token for /v1 endpoints; required, at least 16 characters, for a non-loopback bind
VIGO_PREPAREallModes a single-City stream or serve worker prepares in the background when it opens: all, none, or a comma-separated list of transit, walk, drive and bike. Transit activates today's timetable in the City's timezone; walk loads the pedestrian hierarchy while no request is waiting; drive and bike open their networks. A request waits only for the part it needs. Collections prepare on first use
RAYON_NUM_THREADSAvailable CPUsThreads used inside one query
VIGO_MAX_RESIDENT_SCENARIOSCollection's maximumResidentScenarios1–16 collection members kept loaded
VIGO_RESIDENT_HEAP_BYTESmin(1 GiB, memory ÷ 3)Retained-heap budget for a collection's resident members; not a process memory limit
VIGO_TIMETABLE_CACHE_BYTES128 MiB, growing; see Runtime memoryBudget for inactive scheduled timetables; 0 disables retention
VIGO_ENDPOINT_CACHE_MAX_BYTES64 MiB per endpoint role, or ÷ 64 of memoryEndpoint-access cache budget
VIGO_SHAPE_GEOMETRY_CACHE_MAX_BYTES64 MiB, or ÷ 64 of memoryTransit shape cache budget
VIGO_SHAPE_GEOMETRY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES1024Transit shape cache entries
VIGO_IDLE_RELEASE_MS30000After this idle time, a single-City stream frees street search scratch; 0 keeps it

VIGO_MEMORY_ACCOUNTINGOff1 adds result-tree memory accounting to memory diagnostics; slows queries
VIGO_BIKE_TRACEOffAny value prints bicycle preparation and search timings to standard error


The bicycle index lives in the user cache directory (~/Library/Caches/VIGO on macOS, $XDG_CACHE_HOME/vigo or ~/.cache/vigo on Linux, %LOCALAPPDATA%\VIGO\Cache on Windows). It is derived from the City, holds graph data only, and can be deleted at any time.


vigo build also reads these variables. The routing variables change the prepared City and its policy identity; leave them unset for comparable Cities.

Public results

On this page
Version policyRead a ResultRouteJourneyLegsNo journeyKeep uncertainty with the answerMatrixReachCompare saved resultsDistributionsErrorsDiagnosticsMetadata and reproducibilityKeep a reproducible run
The engine, the compiler, the resident stream and the HTTP API return one public Result format. This page explains how to read it. The API schema lists every field with its type, generated from the engine's result types.


Version policy


Each Result names its schema: vigo.route.v1, vigo.matrix.v1, vigo.reach.v1, vigo.compare.v1, vigo.distribution.v1 or vigo.error.v1. Within a v1 schema, required fields keep their names, types, units and meanings; new optional fields may appear. Removing or renaming a field, changing a unit, or changing a status meaning requires a new schema version. Clients should ignore fields they do not know.


trace, native operations and Studio's internal messages are outside this policy. Result schema versions are independent of the City format and of the executable version, which meta.engineVersion reports.


Read a Result


Read status first:


statusMeaningExit code / HTTP
okThe query completed with an answer0 / 200
not_foundA valid outcome: nothing satisfies the request (Route)0 / 200
errorThe request was invalid or failed; see error2 / 4xx or 5xx


Every Route, Matrix and Reach Result also carries:


FieldMeaning
schemaThe schema name and version
modetransit, walk, drive or bike; for transit, the mode actually returned can be walk
queryThe normalized request: places in public form, serviceDate, requestedTime, timePreference, dataMode
metaHow the Result was computed; see Metadata and reproducibility
warningsQualifications of the answer, each with a code and a message; absent when none
id, sequenceThe caller's id, and the line number on a stream
scenarioIdThe collection member used, when the City is a collection
accessibilityThe wheelchair profile, its street evidence and limitations, in a wheelchair City
datasetLimitationsThe City's limitations, with includeLimitations: true


In a terminal, Route prints a short itinerary. Pipes, --output and --format json produce JSON; --format text asks for the terminal view.


Route


vigo.route.v1 holds one journey, or null when status is not_found.


Journey


FieldMeaning
departureTime, arrivalTimeService-day clocks, HH:MM:SS; hours can exceed 23
clockDateThe date those clocks count from; null for a walk or drive without a service date
durationSecondsArrival minus departure
walkingSeconds, ridingSeconds, waitingSecondsTime walking, on vehicles, and in the gaps before and between legs
drivingSeconds, cyclingSecondsTime driving or cycling, in those modes
boardings, transfersVehicles boarded; transfers is boardings − 1
legsThe chronological legs
expandedWalkingLimitKmPresent on a choice found with a wider walking limit


Durations are whole seconds, rounded at the public boundary; the search keeps full precision. Waiting is the gaps between legs, not a reliability margin. An arrive-by journey can arrive before the deadline.


alternatives holds further distinct journeys, without the primary or duplicates, and is omitted when there are none. alternativeSearch records how they were found: requested alternatives (coverage: "requested_time") or a journey window (with its sampling direction). See alternative journeys and journey windows.


Legs


Every leg has type, from, to, departureTime, arrivalTime, durationSeconds, an optional distanceMeters, optional GeoJSON geometry, and a quality.


typeLeg
walkA continuous walk; street and station pieces are listed in components
transitOne ride on one trip
drive, bikeDriving or cycling


from and to are places: a coordinate, plus stop and name at a stop. Stops, routes, trips and services are identifiers of the form {"feed": "mbta", "id": "70067"}; feed is null in a single-feed City. Requests accept the same form, {"stop": {"feed": "mbta", "id": "70067"}}, or the plain {"stopId": "70067"}.


A transit leg adds route (with id, shortName, longName, type and color), trip, service, serviceDate, headsign, tripShortName, directionId and intermediateStops with their times. It can also carry:


  • fare: the published fare for a new boarding (status: "published", with the fare standard, options and source), or why there is none (status: "unavailable", with a code such as missing_catalog or no_rule, and a reason). See Published fares.
  • alerts: Service Alerts active during the ride, from a realtime snapshot.
  • continuation: {"type": "stay_aboard", "durationSeconds": 300} when an explicit GTFS link keeps the rider aboard from the previous leg. That time is riding, not waiting.
  • quality.flex: the assumptions and booking rules of a GTFS Flex ride.


Geometry is included by default for Route (includeGeometry: false omits it) and is opt-in for Matrix journeys. A transit line runs from the boarding stop along the aligned GTFS shape to the alighting stop, and its distanceMeters is that line's length. Geometry is the modeled path, not a vehicle trace or a surveyed station interior. If any piece of a walk lacks geometry, the leg omits its line rather than drawing across the gap.


journey.sharedLegAlternatives appears with sharedLegs: true; its options and frequencies are described in shared-leg services. Their legIndex values refer to this leg list.


No journey


A not_found Route has journey: null, a reason with code and message, and an access report for each end that explains how far walking reached. When no journey is found lists the codes. A not_found Result is a complete answer: keep it, and never replace it with zero.


Keep uncertainty with the answer


Each leg's quality says what its evidence is:


FieldValues
Transit quality.geometrygtfs_shape (aligned to the feed's shape), stop_sequence (straight lines between stops) or unknown
Transit quality.scheduletimetable (scheduled times), source_time_limitations (the feed repeats times or bridges untimed stops), realtime (an applied prediction) or flex_estimate
Walk quality.geometrySourceosm, osm_and_station_path, gtfs_pathway, station_selection, unverified_transfer or unknown
Walk quality.streetGeometryverified when the street part is a path in the prepared graph, otherwise unverified
Walk quality.stationPathsource_path (declared pathways) or inferred (an assumed station link)
Walk quality.stationTimeestimated when untimed stairs or gates use VIGO's estimates


A verified street path does not certify a complete entrance-to-platform path, and timetable means scheduled, not observed, times. A walk that starts or ends off the street network reports the straight hop as endpointConnector, with streetPathVerified: false. components separates street and station costs and names their sources. Walking evidence explains station costs.


No warnings does not certify complete source coverage. City-level limitations are in vigo info and GET /v1/info, or in a Result with includeLimitations: true; unsupported GTFS features are in Known limits.


Matrix


vigo.matrix.v1 returns durationsSeconds[origin][destination] in request order, with the endpoints echoed in query. Unreachable cells are null, never zero, and a completed matrix can contain both.


  • Depart-at: seconds from the shared departure to arrival.
  • Arrive-by: seconds from the latest departure to the shared deadline, including any wait after an early arrival. The nested journey shows the actual arrival.
  • journeys[origin][destination]: with includeJourneys: true, a journey or null per cell.
  • distancesMeters: for Walk, Drive and Bike, distances in the same order.
  • access: access reports keyed by endpoint index, when an endpoint could not reach the network.


Reach


vigo.reach.v1 returns:


FieldMeaning
cutoffsSecondsThe cutoffs, sorted
surfacewidth, height, bounds and valuesSeconds, row-major from the northwest cell; null where unreached
fullSurfaceThe same grid over the full reached extent, when it differs
areas, contoursGeoJSON FeatureCollections for the requested grid; each feature names its cutoff
fullAreas, fullContoursThe same for the full extent
stopsReached stops and when; scenarioStops lists stops a scenario added
surface.edges, surface.nodesStreet evidence with includeStreetEdges and includeNodes
allDayThe sample count and window of an all-day Reach


Cell order is row-major from the northwest; Read the surface gives the cell-center formula. Areas are cumulative: the 30-minute area includes the 15-minute area.


With reachFormat: "map", the Result contains only areas and bounds for the full reached extent; its polygons equal fullAreas of the default format. With reachFormat: "surface", polygons and contours are not built. Use the full format for comparisons.


Compare saved results


vigo.compare.v1 reports changes between two saved Results without routing again. Changes are after minus before, in seconds.


FamilyFields
RoutedurationChangeSeconds and transferChange; null when either Result has no journey
Matrix, Reachcounts (comparable, faster, slower, unchanged, newlyReachable, noLongerReachable) and meanChangeSeconds


beforeStatus, afterStatus and cityRevisions identify the inputs. meanChangeSeconds averages only entries reachable in both, and is null when there are none; new and lost reachability are counted separately. Matrix comparison requires identical ordered endpoints, and Reach comparison the same grid. Compare does not check that dates, times, modes or walking limits match: align them yourself. The engine compares Reach only; the compiler also compares Route and Matrix.


Distributions


vigo.distribution.v1 is returned by a Route, Matrix or Reach request with monteCarlo. durationsSeconds[p] holds the p-th requested percentile for every destination or cell, with null meaning unreachable in that share of samples. reachableSamples counts finite outcomes. sampling and assumptions record the method. See Monte Carlo.


Errors


vigo.error.v1 has status: "error" and error with a code and a message. Handle the code and the HTTP status, never the message text. Codes include invalid_request, stop_not_found, scenario_not_found, unsupported_mode, file_not_found, permission_denied and city_unavailable, and transport codes such as unauthorized, request_timeout, query_timeout, query_canceled, request_id_conflict and service_unavailable. On a stream, an error is one output line and later lines still run.


Diagnostics


LevelAdds
none (default)Nothing
summarydiagnostics: search counters and candidate counts
profileAlso profile.timingsUs: measured timings in microseconds
traceAlso trace: the full internal result


Set the level with --diagnostics, a diagnostics field, or the ?diagnostics= (also ?vigo_diagnostics=) query parameter; conflicting values are rejected. Counters without instrumentation are omitted, never invented. scannedDepartures, expandedTripRuns and relaxedStops count algorithm work, not network size or distinct stops. Profile scopes can overlap; never add them. summary and profile describe each runtime's own instrumentation and are not comparable across runtimes.


trace is an unstable debugging interface: internal indices, sentinels and duplicate units stay there. The trace reference documents it. stream --stream-output=detailed returns the same trace in a vigo.stream.detail.v1 envelope without building the public Result; its status: "ok" means execution completed, so read the trace's own routing status. Clients must check that capabilities.output.streamFormats lists detailed; VIGO Python does this automatically.


Metadata and reproducibility


meta records how a Result was computed:


FieldMeaning
engineVersionThe executable's version
cityRevisionThe City build used
requestIdThe caller's id, or a generated identifier
queryFingerprintHash of the complete request (stop references canonicalized, output switches excluded), the City revision and the engine version
assumptionsFingerprintHash of the routing assumptions, without scenario and observation content
scenarioFingerprint, realtimeSnapshotFingerprintHashes of supplied scenario and realtime content
computeUs, computeScopeMicroseconds for service-date activation, search and Result construction (query_dispatch_including_materialization); excludes formatting, serialization, queueing and the network
realtime, trafficAdmission and coverage of supplied observations


The query fingerprint includes scenario content, via points, alternative settings and the identity of an admitted live snapshot, and excludes id, diagnostics, includeGeometry, includeLimitations and reachFormat. Equivalent requests written differently, such as time and timeMinutes, can hash differently. Compare Results only when their assumptionsFingerprint values match, or when you have checked the differing assumptions yourself. Server-Timing headers report serialization, compute and, on the engine, queue time; measure client wall time separately.


Keep a reproducible run


Keep together: the City (or its revision and sources), the original request, the executable version and capabilities, any supplied scenario, realtime snapshot or traffic, and the complete Result. The query echo and the fingerprints identify these inputs but do not archive them. For a source-data audit, also keep a diagnostics: "trace" Result.


Python Results use ready and blocked, minutes, and their own properties; see the Python Results guide.

Trace output
1 min readSource
diagnostics: "trace" adds the engine's internal result under trace, and stream --stream-output=detailed returns it in a vigo.stream.detail.v1 envelope. This page documents that internal object for debugging and research tools. It is not part of the stable public schema: fields, units and sentinels can change between releases. Applications should read the public results.


Read the outcome first, then the journey or analysis values. Keep units, array order and provenance with the values.


Timing and metadata


FieldMeaning
schemaVersionvigo.standalone.result.v1; Compare uses vigo.standalone.comparison.v1. Identifies the JSON interface, not the executable
runtimerust
cityRevisionRevision of the loaded City; IDs and indices depend on it
timing.totalMsMilliseconds inside dispatch, including on-demand preparation and result construction. Excludes City loading, process startup, serialization, HTTP queueing and client parsing
timing.timetableSourceprepared_snapshot when a compiled service timetable was reused, source when it was prepared from SQLite
idEchoed by the stream and HTTP when supplied
warningsSource limitations affecting the answer; may be absent, null or an array


The object is the result itself, without a data wrapper. Native results put their object under result, next to operation. Member order has no meaning; accept unknown fields.


Trace outcomeMeaningHandling
Route status: "ready"A journey was computedRead legs or segments; display the returned mode
Route status: "blocked"No admissible journeyRead reason; journey fields may be absent
Matrix cell nullNo finite durationKeep it null; exclude it from averages
Reach cell nullNo value reachedNever convert to zero


The public Route uses ok and not_found for these outcomes.

Route output
4 min readSource
On this page
Journey clocks and totalsRead the leg sequenceGeometry and evidenceDirect, via, window and blocked variants
A trace Route describes one journey, a sequence through via points, or sampled window choices. Read status, then look for segments or choices.


Journey clocks and totals


For the reference fixture, the following fields are exact; legs, diagnostics and metadata are omitted:


JSON
{
  "status": "ready",
  "mode": "transit",
  "departureMinutes": 475,
  "arrivalMinutes": 510,
  "durationMinutes": 35,
  "boardings": 2,
  "transfers": 1,
  "walkMinutes": 0,
  "rideMinutes": 25,
  "waitMinutes": 10
}


FieldMeaning
departureMinutesJourney start in minutes after service-day midnight. Depart-at starts at the requested clock; arrive-by at the latest departure
arrivalMinutesJourney end on the same clock; arrive-by can finish before the deadline
durationMinutesarrivalMinutes − departureMinutes
boardingsTransit boardings
transfersmax(boardings − 1, 0); zero for a direct walk or drive
walkMinutesTime on non-ride legs, including modeled access and transfer allowances
rideMinutesSum of ride legs
waitMinutesThe rest: gaps before the first boarding and between rides
departure, arrivalNative service-day clocks in seconds
walkingSeconds, rideSeconds, waitingSecondsNative counterparts of the totals


Here 475 is 07:55, 510 is 08:30, and 35 = 0 + 25 + 10. Values can be fractional. Clocks can exceed 1440 minutes: 1500 is 25:00 on the selected service day. Keep the date offset; never take the clock modulo 24 hours.


Read the leg sequence


legs runs from origin to destination. Waiting is a gap between legs, not a leg. The fixture route has two zero-length station-selection walks around two rides:


StepClockMeaning
Access07:55 → 07:55Selected stop A; no physical walk requested
Gap07:55 → 08:00Five minutes before the first boarding
Ride T108:00 → 08:10A → X
Gap08:10 → 08:15Five minutes before the next ride
Ride T208:15 → 08:30X → B
Egress08:30 → 08:30Selected destination B


The first ride, legs[1], with other properties omitted:


JSON
{
  "kind": "ride",
  "tripId": "T1",
  "routeId": "R1",
  "fromStopId": "A",
  "toStopId": "X",
  "departureMinutes": 480,
  "arrivalMinutes": 490,
  "durationMinutes": 10,
  "stopIds": ["A", "X"],
  "stopCount": 1,
  "geometrySource": "stop_sequence",
  "coordinates": [[-77.05, 38.9], [-77.04, 38.905]]
}


Leg fieldMeaning
kindride or walk in transit; walk for a direct walk; drive between optional walk legs for a drive
from, toEndpoint objects with coordinate, plus stopId and name at a stop. Direct street legs omit them
fromStopId, toStopIdStop IDs at stop endpoints
fromStop, toStop, tripIndices into the active native timetable, not GTFS IDs
tripId, routeId, routeRide identity and route display data (shortName, longName, type, color)
boardSequence, alightSequenceNative connection sequence values; not offsets into stopIds or GTFS stop_sequence
stopIdsThe ride's stops, including boarding and alighting
stopCountstopIds.length − 1
coordinates[longitude, latitude] pairs; plain arrays, not GeoJSON
distanceMetersLength of the returned line, not necessarily the operator's distance


Walk legs keep their access cost. When it includes a station connection, accessCost.street and accessCost.station separate distances and seconds, and the station part lists directed stop IDs and sources. A published transfer minimum is timing, not a path. stationAccessStatus: "unverified" and streetPathVerified: false keep that uncertainty; streetSegmentVerified describes only the street part; a source-backed pathway reports stationAccessStatus: "source_path". unverifiedStationAccessLegs counts unresolved station connections.


Geometry and evidence


geometrySourceWhat the line is
gtfs_shapeThe GTFS shape, aligned and cut between the stops
stop_sequenceA line through stop coordinates; need not follow the street or track
osmA walking path in the prepared street graph
osm_and_station_pathA street path joined to a station path
gtfs_pathwayA GTFS pathway transfer between located stops
stop_coordinate_fallbackA transfer priced by a GTFS transfer rule, drawn between the stops
station_selectionA selected-stop connector; no street path was checked
unverified_transferA transfer without a materialized path, such as between platforms of one station
coordinate-snapThe straight walk between a free point and its road (drives)


streetPathVerified: true marks a walking leg verified on the graph; the fallback labels set it to false. Missing does not mean false; ride legs do not use it. Graph verification does not establish wheelchair access, station-interior access or fare eligibility. Matrix journeys include geometry only with includeGeometry.


Direct, via, window and blocked variants


Direct Walk Results have one street leg; Drive Results have a drive leg with walk legs where a point lies off its road. Both report distanceMeters, clocks and transfers: 0, and omit transit totals. A transit request with requireTransitRide: false can return mode: "walk": display the returned mode.


Via routes have ordered segments and a total duration, without a flattened legs array or aggregate totals. Window routes have the selected journey at the top level and up to five choices in choices; window.searches counts sampled times, not choices.


Reversing the fixture route to B → A gives exactly:


JSON
{"status": "blocked", "mode": "transit", "reason": "no_path"}


ReasonMeaning
no_accessAn endpoint has no admissible transit candidate
no_pathNo path under the request's constraints
before_service_dayA direct street arrive-by would need a negative departure clock
no_drivable_road_within_walkNo drivable road within maxWalkKm of an endpoint
via_leg_blockedA via segment failed; see legIndex and leg

Matrix output
1 min readSource
On this page
Rows, columns and nullsDepart-at and arrive-by durationsJourney detail
A trace Matrix is indexed by the request's origins and destinations. It returns counts, not the endpoints themselves: keep the request with it.


Rows, columns and nulls


The Matrix example uses origins [A, X] and destinations [B, A]:


JSON
{
  "kind": "matrix",
  "mode": "transit",
  "originCount": 2,
  "destinationCount": 2,
  "durationsMinutes": [[35, null], [35, null]]
}


Destination BDestination A
Origin A35 minutesUnreachable
Origin X35 minutesUnreachable


durationsMinutes[1][0] is X → B: 20 minutes waiting and 15 riding from 07:55. A → A is null because the request requires a ride and no service returns. Never fill the diagonal with zero, and test duration !== null, not truthiness.


Depart-at and arrive-by durations


depart-at: duration = (arrival clock - requested departure clock) / 60
arrive-by: duration = (requested deadline - latest departure clock) / 60


Clocks are in seconds. For A → B with an 08:40 deadline, the cell is 40 minutes: from the 08:00 latest departure to the deadline. The journey itself arrives at 08:30 and takes 30 minutes. Both are intended; the ten minutes are slack before the deadline, not part of the journey.


Journey detail


RequestReturned
Transit, includeJourneys: falsejourneys: null; durations only
Transit, includeJourneys: truejourneys[row][column]; null where unreachable
includeGeometry: falseClocks, legs, IDs and stops without lines
includeGeometry: trueLines and provenance on transit legs
journeyFormat: "compact"Timed trip and stop witnesses without display metadata
A direct walk winsA mode: "walk" journey with one timed leg
Walk, Drive or Bike matrixdistancesMeters and durations; no journeys


Journey cells have the Route journey fields but no status, mode or dispatch metadata. diagnostics.times is the native flat array of clocks in seconds, at offset row * destinationCount + column; it is not the duration matrix, especially where a direct walk replaced transit. Use the timetable.matrix native operation for raw native journeys.

Reach output
4 min readSource
On this page
Main fieldsDecode the rasterAreas and contoursDecode directed street evidence
A trace Reach returns reached stops, rasters, GeoJSON and optional street evidence.


Main fields


FieldMeaning
kind, mode, origin, serviceDatereach, the mode, the origin and the date (null for walking without one). Arrive-by has destination and timePreference: "arrive_by"
cutoffsMinutesSorted, deduplicated cutoffs
stopsStops reached within the largest cutoff, with stopId, name, coordinate and durationMinutes; empty for walk-only Reach
surfaceGrid dimensions, requested and full rasters, and optional evidence
areas, fullAreasMultiPolygon features for the requested and full rasters
contours, fullContoursMultiLineString features
diagnosticsTransit search and street surface evidence


Stop durations are minutes after the query clock (before the deadline for arrive-by). Stops follow timetable order, not duration; sort them yourself.


Decode the raster


surface.width * surface.height equals surface.values.length; index zero is the northwest cell, x grows east and y grows south. With street sampling a value is the least time on the reached streets in the cell; with cell-center sampling it is the Matrix time to the center. This function reads a cell without confusing zero with null:


JavaScript
function readCell(surface, x, y) {
  const { width, height, bounds, values } = surface;
  if (!Number.isInteger(x) || !Number.isInteger(y) ||
      x < 0 || x >= width || y < 0 || y >= height) {
    throw new RangeError('Cell is outside the raster');
  }
  const [west, south, east, north] = bounds;
  return {
    index: y * width + x,
    coordinate: [
      west + (x + 0.5) / width * (east - west),
      north - (y + 0.5) / height * (north - south)
    ],
    durationMinutes: values[y * width + x]
  };
}


A cell belongs to a cutoff when its value is not null and at most that cutoff. For the full raster, pass {...surface, bounds: surface.fullBounds, values: surface.fullValues}; when no separate surface exists, the full pair repeats the requested one. Changing bounds at fixed dimensions changes cell size, so equal indices need not mean the same place.


Areas and contours


GeometryCoordinates
MultiPolygoncoordinates[polygon][ring][vertex]; ring zero is the exterior, later rings are holes
MultiLineStringcoordinates[line][vertex]


Cutoff areas are cumulative: the 30-minute area includes the 15-minute area, so never add them. A cutoff with no geometry has no feature; match features by cutoffMinutes. Areas trace occupied cells; contours interpolate crossings. Both depend on resolution. Measure area with a projected or geodesic method, not in degrees.


Decode directed street evidence


With includeStreetEdges: true, surface.edges has schemaVersion: "vigo.standalone.street-edges.v2" and encoding: "indexed-json"; otherwise it is null.


FieldMeaning
countNumber of directed intervals
nodeCount, nodesLocal coordinate table: nodes.length = 2 * nodeCount, longitude then latitude
endpointsTwo local node indices per interval, from then to
edgeIdsPrepared directed edge IDs; not portable between Cities
durationMinutes, fromDurationMinutesMinutes at the interval's end and start
startFractions, endFractionsInterval limits along the edge, 0–1
walkDistanceMWalking distance from the seed through this interval, including snapping
transitArrivalMinutesArrival at the transit seed; -1 marks the direct-origin seed


Repeated edge IDs are ordered, non-overlapping intervals; opposite directions are separate. For a smaller cutoff, clip an interval at the cutoff instead of dropping it. In arrive-by Reach, times are minutes before the deadline and still grow from from to to, while the traveler walks the other way; -1 marks the destination seed. This decoder reads both directions:


JavaScript
function readEdge(bundle, i, cutoffMinutes = Infinity) {
  if (!Number.isInteger(i) || i < 0 || i >= bundle.count) {
    throw new RangeError('Edge is outside the bundle');
  }
  const point = node => bundle.nodes.slice(2 * node, 2 * node + 2);
  const from = point(bundle.endpoints[2 * i]);
  const to = point(bundle.endpoints[2 * i + 1]);
  const start = bundle.startFractions?.[i] ?? 0;
  const end = bundle.endFractions?.[i] ?? 1;
  const startTime = bundle.fromDurationMinutes?.[i] ?? bundle.durationMinutes[i];
  const endTime = bundle.durationMinutes[i];
  if (cutoffMinutes < startTime) return null;
  const clippedEnd = endTime <= cutoffMinutes ? end
    : start + (end - start) * (cutoffMinutes - startTime) / (endTime - startTime);
  if (clippedEnd <= start) return null;
  const coordinate = fraction => from.map((v, axis) => v + fraction * (to[axis] - v));
  const seed = bundle.transitArrivalMinutes[i];
  return {
    edgeId: bundle.edgeIds[i],
    coordinates: [coordinate(start), coordinate(clippedEnd)],
    durationMinutes: Math.min(endTime, cutoffMinutes),
    walkDistanceM: bundle.walkDistanceM[i],
    transitArrivalMinutes: seed === -1 ? null : seed
  };
}


The decoder turns the -1 sentinel into null for display; the array keeps -1. Check diagnostics.surface.edgeEvidenceTruncated before treating the records as complete. surface.nodes is a separate list of reached nodes (longitude, latitude, durationMinutes, walkDistanceM), empty unless includeNodes: true, capped at 30,000 with diagnostics.surface.nodeEvidenceTruncated.

On this page
Signs and reachabilityGrid and provenance
Compare reads the requested surface.values of two Reach traces; it ignores full rasters, areas, stops and edges.


Signs and reachability


BeforeAfterDeltaCounted as
NumberNumberAfter minus beforecommonCells
NullNumberNullnewlyReachableCells
NumberNullNullnoLongerReachableCells
NullNullNullNot counted


For these illustrative arrays, not network times:


before = [10, null, 20, null]
after  = [ 8,   15, null, null]


the comparator returns exactly:


JSON
{
  "kind": "compare",
  "schemaVersion": "vigo.standalone.comparison.v1",
  "sign": "after-minus-before",
  "commonCells": 1,
  "newlyReachableCells": 1,
  "noLongerReachableCells": 1,
  "meanChangeMinutes": -2,
  "deltaMinutes": [-2, null, null, null]
}


meanChangeMinutes averages common cells only, and is null when there are none. Never replace null deltas with zero. Cells unreachable in both number width * height − commonCells − newlyReachableCells − noLongerReachableCells.


Grid and provenance


The result carries width, height and bounds; deltaMinutes uses the Reach cell order. Fix bounds explicitly when running a baseline and a scenario so cells line up. The outer cityRevision is the loaded City's; the comparator checks only that the two inputs agree with each other.

Diagnostics and native output
1 min readSource
ResultDiagnostics
Transit Routediagnostics.originAccess, destinationAccess, search, native and realtime
Walk or Drive RouteThe native street or drive result
Transit MatrixThe native timetable matrix result
Walk or Drive MatrixThe native street or drive matrix result
Reachdiagnostics.transit (null for walk-only) and diagnostics.surface
Via RoutePer-segment diagnostics under segments


Transit search diagnostics report startSeconds, endSeconds, the transfer policy and horizonScope: "timetable_scan". When a direct walk wins a transit request, the native diagnostics still describe the transit search; never overwrite the returned value with a diagnostic clock.


queryNs / 1_000_000 converts a native query time to milliseconds; it is a kernel scope, not latency. Do not sum nested timings. scannedDepartures, expandedTripRuns and relaxedStops count algorithm work, not distinct trips or stops. reachedPixels counts finite cells; reachedEdgeCount and reachedEdgeLengthM count directed edges, so a two-way street counts twice.


Native responses contain operation and a typed result. Native fields are always present; unavailable optional values are null. Timetable operations index into the arrays of timetable.identifiers for the same service date and policy; never reuse saved indices across preparations. Native timetable.matrix returns a flat origin-major times array of service-day clock seconds: for the fixture's A → B, [30600], an 08:30 arrival.

Reference
VIGO compiler
5 min readSource
On this page
InstallCommandsBuild a CityRun a queryKeep the compiler residentCompare saved ResultsPackage and verify
The compiler, vigo.mjs, builds Cities and scenario collections from GTFS and OpenStreetMap, and runs Route, Matrix, Reach, Stream and Compare against them. Its build and build-scenarios run the engine's vigo build and vigo build-scenarios with the same arguments, so they write the same Cities; the engine, the compiler and Python open them.


The compiler archive (VIGO-CLI-…) contains vigo.mjs, its native routing kernel vigo-routing-kernel.node, the vigo executable it uses to build Cities and answer queries, license notices and a checksum manifest. It needs Node.js 24.18 or newer on the matching operating system and CPU, and bundles neither Node nor City data.


Install


Extract the archive from VIGO releases, keep its files together, and run:


Shell
node vigo.mjs --version
node vigo.mjs capabilities
node vigo.mjs help route


No npm installation, Rust compiler or Studio is needed. The guides call the compiler vigo-build. In a POSIX shell:


Shell
alias vigo-build='node "/absolute/path/to/vigo.mjs"'


On Windows, use node .\vigo.mjs, or define your own function. From a source checkout, npm run build:cli-runtime builds public/vigo.mjs and its kernel.


Commands


CommandInputOutput
buildGTFS, OSM and an output directoryA complete City; its manifest on standard output
build-scenariosA scenario source manifestA scenario collection
capabilitiesNoneVersions and supported combinations, as JSON
inspectA CityIdentity, sources, counts and limitations
routeA City and a JSON request, or a CSV batchA Route Result
matrixA City and a JSON requestA Matrix Result
reachA City and a JSON requestA Reach Result, computed by the vigo executable
streamA City, and NDJSON on standard inputOne Result per line from a resident process
compareTwo saved ResultsChanges, without routing again


vigo-build help COMMAND or vigo-build COMMAND -h prints every option with its default. Options accept --name value and --name=value. Unknown options, extra arguments and repeated single-value options are rejected; --gtfs, --gtfs-scope and --prepare-date may repeat.


Build a City


Shell
vigo-build build --gtfs feed.zip --osm region.osm.pbf --output ./city
vigo-build inspect --city ./city


OptionMeaning
--gtfs PATHGTFS ZIP; repeat for several feeds
--gtfs-scope NAMEA unique, stable scope for each --gtfs
--osm PATHOSM .pbf covering the City
--output PATHThe City directory to write
--street-modes VALUEwalk,drive (default), walk, walk,bike or walk,drive,bike
--prepare-date YYYY-MM-DDCompile a service date's timetable now; repeat for other dates
--private-access VALUEpublic (default) or endpoints
--wheelchairBuild a strict wheelchair City
--wheelchair-streets MODEinferred (default) or verified street evidence for a wheelchair City
--streets-from PATHReuse identical prepared streets from another City
--replaceReplace an existing City


Build a City explains each option, combining feeds, large regions and low-memory builds. The quickstart has a complete Boston example. Progress goes to standard error. vigo.mjs runs the vigo executable beside it, which stages and publishes the City; set VIGO_STANDALONE_PATH to use another one. A signal sent to vigo.mjs reaches the build, and the build stops if vigo.mjs is killed.


Run a query


Requests carry serviceDate and time in JSON; flags override request fields.


Shell
vigo-build route --city ./city --request route.json --output result.json
cat route.json | vigo-build route --city ./city --request - --time 08:30 > result.json


OptionCommandsMeaning
--city PATHQuery commandsThe City
--request PATHroute, matrix, reachJSON request; - reads standard input
--output PATHMost commandsSave the JSON; it is also printed. - prints only
--service-date YYYY-MM-DDQuery commandsService date
--service-day VALUEQuery commandsweekday, saturday or sunday; must agree with the date
--time HH:MMQuery commandsClock, 00:00–29:59 (default 08:00)
--time-preference depart|arriveroute, matrix, reachTime direction; JSON also accepts depart_at and arrive_by
--mode VALUEroute, matrix, reachtransit (default), walk, drive or bike
--objective earliest_arrivalroute, matrix, reachThe only objective
--max-walk KMQuery commandsWalking budget (default 1.2)
--max-transfers Nroute, matrix, reachTransfer cap, 0–31
--horizon MINroute, matrixTimetable horizon, 1–2880 (default 480)
--departure-window MINrouteCentered depart-at window, ±0–30 whole minutes
--alternatives N, --alternative-rankingrouteAdditional transit journeys and their ranking
--data-mode scheduled|realtimerouteRealtime needs a realtimeSnapshot in the request
--cutoffs, --extent-radius, --raster-size, --walk-speed, --street-edgesreachReach options
--input PATHrouteA CSV batch of transit journeys; needs --output
--wheelchairQuery commandsRequire a wheelchair City
--diagnostics LEVELQuery commandsnone, summary, profile or trace
--format text|jsonroute, matrix, reachTerminal text or JSON
--include-geometry, --include-limitationsQuery commandsOutput detail


Request files and standard input share a 16 MiB limit, and --request - reads until the producer closes standard input. Results go to standard output; progress and errors to standard error. Saved output is written to a temporary file and renamed, so a failed run can leave an older file in place: check the exit code. Exit 0 means a Result, including not_found; exit 2 means invalid input or a failure.


The request format is the engine's, documented in the engine reference, with these differences:


FeatureCompilerEngine
Matrix size100,000 pairs in 16 MiB65,536 pairs in 8 MiB
Departure windowsdepartureWindowMinutes, centered ±0–30windowMinutes, later departures or earlier deadlines
RealtimeRoute onlyRoute, Matrix and Reach
Planned scenariosReachReach and transit Route
Reach raster sizes48, 64, 96, 128, 192, 256, 384, 512 or 1024Any integer 16–1024
CompareRoute, Matrix and ReachReach
CSV route batches--inputNot available


Matrix points may also use the older {"id": "a", "point": "A"} form, which the engine rejects. CSV batches take columns id, origin_lon, origin_lat, destination_lon, destination_lat, or origin_stop_id and destination_stop_id, with optional origin_name and destination_name.


Keep the compiler resident


stream reads one request per line, each with a kind (route, matrix or reach) and an optional id, and keeps the City prepared between lines. Each line may choose its own serviceDate; --service-date only sets the default.


NDJSON
{"id":"outbound","kind":"route","origin":{"stopId":"A"},"destination":{"stopId":"B"},"serviceDate":"2026-10-05","time":"08:00"}
{"id":"times","kind":"matrix","origins":[{"stopId":"A"}],"destinations":[{"stopId":"B"}],"serviceDate":"2026-10-05","time":"08:00"}


Shell
vigo-build stream --city ./city < queries.ndjson > results.ndjson


Responses echo id, add sequence, and keep input order. A failed line returns status: "error" and later lines still run; read every status, even on exit 0. --workers N (1–4, default 1) runs several resident workers, capped by CPU and memory (two CPUs and 6 GiB each); each loads its own City. --stream-output detailed returns the internal trace envelope.


Compare saved Results


Shell
vigo-build compare --before before.json --after after.json --output change.json


Both Results must be from the same query family; Reach Results must share a grid. Changes are after minus before. See Compare saved results.


Package and verify


From a source checkout, npm run package:cli builds the archive and npm run check:cli-package tests the extracted copy. Archives are specific to their platform; keep the manifest when reporting a problem.


For an HTTP service, use the engine. For notebooks and batches, use VIGO Python.

Reference
Native operations
1 min readSource
Native operations call the routing kernels directly with packed arrays. They are diagnostic and research tools outside the public stability policy. Use vigo native --city ./city --request query.json or POST /v1/native with operation, input and, for timetable operations, serviceDate. Native indices belong to the loaded City and service date. The HTTP API never accepts a file path in a query.


JSON
{
  "operation": "timetable.identifiers",
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15"
}


timetable.identifiers returns stopIds, tripIds, routeIds (one per active trip) and accessMemberStopIds. An index is a position in these arrays. Offset arrays start at zero, end at their packed array's length and have one more entry than their groups; parallel arrays must have equal lengths.


A street path needs coordinates only:


JSON
{
  "operation": "street.path",
  "input": {
    "originLon": -77.05,
    "originLat": 38.9,
    "destinationLon": -77.03,
    "destinationLat": 38.91,
    "maximumDistanceM": 5000,
    "maximumPoints": 512
  }
}


Native departure, horizon, earliest and deadline are absolute service-day seconds: native horizon is an end clock, while horizonMinutes is a duration. maximumBoardings is a transfer cap plus one. Walking times and transfer arrays are seconds; distances are meters; drive traffic weights are hundredths of a second. queryNs is nanoseconds.


Native Matrix returns flat clock times in seconds: arrivals for depart-at, departures for arrive-by, null where unreachable. timetable.pareto exposes the arrival, boarding and walking frontier. realtime.compile compiles explicit call times; it does not fetch feeds. places.describe labels up to 256 coordinates with nearby street, area or stop names from the City, in parallel labels and kinds arrays; labels never change routing. timetable.prepare, street.prepare, bike.prepare and drive.prepare load a mode without routing.


The native field reference lists every operation's input and result type, generated from the Rust definitions.

Generated for VIGO 1.0.0 from public Rust structs. Regenerate with npm run docs:standalone.


Native operations are diagnostic tools outside the public stability policy. See native operations for units, index domains and examples. In requests, an optional field accepts omission or null. Result objects include every listed field; an unavailable optional value is null. Native arrays become JSON arrays, and non-finite result numbers become null. The runtime also checks compatible array lengths, indices, and values.
